We compare these taxonomies with the existing Common Core State Standards (CCSS)-based knowledge-component taxonomies in two ASSISTments datasets and evaluate their utility in Deep Knowledge Tracing, a downstream task that relies on taxonomic mappings of questions to knowledge components. The embedding-based taxonomies exhibit substantial but incomplete correspondence with the existing taxonomies, revealing both preserved and alternative organizations of educational content. When used for knowledge tracing, they improve predictive performance by approximately 3-5 AUC percentage points. These results demonstrate the potential of semantic embeddings for automatically constructing educational taxonomies that both recover structure present in human-developed taxonomies and provide useful alternative representations for downstream educational modeling.

papers.title: Scalable Unrolled Chains for MRI Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Unrolled variational networks achieve state-of-the-art performance for accelerated MRI reconstruction, but standard end-to-end training becomes prohibitively memory intensive as the number and width of cascades increase. We propose a memory-efficient training framework that updates a randomly sampled cascade while retaining supervision from the final reconstruction loss. The error signal is propagated from the end of the chain to the sampled cascade using an activation-light backward pass that avoids storing full chain activations, thereby decoupling training memory from chain length. A time-conditioned network shared across cascades further keeps the parameter count independent of chain length. The backward pass is approximate only through frozen normalization statistics, and a trained exact gradient control shows the approximation leaves reconstruction quality unchanged. The framework remains trainable at chain lengths and cascade widths where standard end-to-end backpropagation exhausts GPU memory. On fastMRI single-coil knee and multi-coil brain reconstruction, our method consistently outperforms other local training approaches. On high-SNR knee slices, our method surpasses E2E-VarNet at $8\times$ and matches it at $4\times$, while on the complete brain validation set it surpasses E2E-VarNet at $8\times$ and achieves comparable performance at $4\times$, with fewer parameters, lower peak memory, and faster per-iteration training. Code is available at https://github.com/emehillaj/scalable-unrolled-mri.

papers.title: Noninteger completely monotonic degrees of Stirling remainders and their derivatives
papers.abstract: For Stirling expansions truncated after at least two Bernoulli terms, we disprove the three real-degree conjectures recorded by Mahmoud and Qi for the signed remainders of the logarithm of the gamma function and their derivatives. We give a unified proof of the corresponding integer-degree formula, recovering known cases and resolving Zhu's conjectures for higher derivatives in this range. Every real completely monotonic degree lies strictly between the predicted integer and the next integer. We obtain a universal fractional lower bound through an explicit inverse function and a simpler rational bound valid for every derivative order. A local estimate for the negative part of the Laplace kernel's derivative with respect to its logarithmic variable makes the lower improvement proportional to the reciprocal of the combined truncation and derivative order. Together with a uniform upper bound, this determines the exact order of decay of the fractional excess for each fixed derivative order and for its supremum over all derivative orders. Sharper kernel estimates give stronger bounds for the first two degrees. papers.title: E3tereo: Improving Stereo Matching at Depth Boundaries with Learned Geometric Edges
papers.abstract: Depth boundaries remain a major source of error in stereo matching. For IGEV on Scene Flow, geometric edge pixels account for only 6% of evaluated pixels but about half of the total absolute disparity error. Photometric edges can respond to texture changes without corresponding depth discontinuities, making them unreliable cues for boundary refinement. We propose E3Stereo, which learns geometric edges from disparity supervision and combines these boundary cues with the backbone disparity and image details to predict full-resolution disparity corrections. The same edge map also emphasizes boundary errors during training, while joint optimization allows the edge predictor to adapt to disparity refinement. On the Scene Flow dataset, E3Stereo reduces end-point error (EPE) at depth boundaries by 9.5%-14.3% across RAFT-Stereo, IGEV, and MonSter, while also reducing overall EPE. After fine-tuning, our IGEV-based model improves upon IGEV on all eleven reported metrics across ETH3D, KITTI 2012, and KITTI 2015. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

papers.title: Deep-Microscopic Photonic Bandstructure of a Two-Dimensional Honeycomb Lattice
papers.abstract: Conventional descriptions of light in materials rely on macroscopic models that average the optical response over the microscopic lattice structures. These models are deployed in the semi-classical limit, where the collective local response over many lattice sites is adequate. However, they fail to capture the full spatial dispersion, which requires a lattice-resolved description of light. We address this limitation by formulating a deep-microscopic nonlocal theory of the photon based on the Maxwell Hamiltonian and its characteristic equation. The solution reveals the full spatial dispersion in the form of deep-microscopic photonic bandstructure, and corresponding real-space Bloch field textures. We demonstrate our theory for a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model of a gapped honeycomb lattice. Our framework thus extends photons to the same microscopic footing as electrons or phonons, providing a unified route to studying topology, dissipation, and quantum fluctuations of light in dispersive materials.

papers.title: Quantum Closed Loop Inverse Kinematics Through Hilbert-Space Encoding of Robot Kinematics
papers.abstract: The integration of quantum computing into robotics requires mathematical representations that preserve the geometric structure and configuration dependence of robot motion. This paper introduces a structure-preserving quantum representation of rigid-body transformations and serial-manipulator kinematics, establishing a correspondence between classical kinematic models and parameterized quantum circuits. Building on the Bloch-sphere representation, spatial directions are encoded into single-qubit states, while quantum rotations reproduce the ordered composition of reference-frame transformations. Translational contributions are combined through quantum-state aggregation, with their metric scales retained classically, enabling the reconstruction of end-effector position and orientation from Pauli expectation values. The formulation preserves the original joint variables and accommodates different kinematic conventions and joint types. Beyond forward kinematics, we establish that the manipulator geometric Jacobian can be reconstructed from quantum-observable derivatives using the parameter-shift rule, with analytical equivalence to its classical counterpart under ideal readout. To demonstrate the applicability of this representation to robot-level algorithms, we introduce Quantum Closed Loop Inverse Kinematics, a hybrid closed-loop method that exploits quantum-derived pose and Jacobian information. The proposed framework provides a geometrically interpretable foundation for developing and investigating quantum and hybrid computational methods for robotic kinematics and motion.

papers.title: Floor Friction Assessment from Robot Tire-Surface Interaction
papers.abstract: Floor traction influences wheel-slip behavior, dead-reckoning accuracy, and the navigation performance of wheeled mobile robots that rely on wheel odometry. As these robots become increasingly common in GNSS-denied indoor environments, including automated manufacturing and retail facilities, their onboard measurements could also be used to characterize floor conditions and improve localization. In this study, a skid-steer robot was driven over five floor surfaces with distinct traction characteristics using commanded velocity profiles designed to induce wheel slip through repeated acceleration and direction reversal. Differences between the body velocity estimated from inertial sensing and the velocity obtained from wheel odometry were evaluated using the integrated relative-velocity error, phase-derived wheel-to-body response delay, and velocity-reversal response delay. Welch power spectral density analysis was additionally applied to characterize the frequency distribution of the velocity mismatch during positive and negative acceleration. Band-integrated spectral power, spectral centroid, and spectral decay rate were extracted from each recording and evaluated using linear discriminant analysis and multiclass classification. The response-delay measurements produced consistent surface-dependent trends, with the longest delays observed on soap and the shortest delays observed on carpet. The spectral features also provided clear separation among the tested surfaces, achieving a balanced classification accuracy of 97.1% under recording-level cross-validation. These results demonstrate that both the magnitude and frequency domain characteristics of wheel-to-body velocity mismatch contain useful information about tire-surface interactions. Such information could support surface recognition and the development of slip-aware wheel-odometry weighting within robot state-estimation frameworks.

papers.title: A Distribution-Matching Perspective on LLM Training Algorithms
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a unified framework for training algorithms across different stages of modern large language model development, based on the perspective of distribution matching. We show that a broad class of language model training algorithms can be interpreted as minimizing a certain divergence between the current model and a target distribution, and that characterizing the properties of this target distribution provides substantial insight into the behavior of the corresponding training algorithms. By analyzing specific forms of the target distribution, we establish that On-Policy Distillation (OPD) enjoys an advantage over classical Knowledge Distillation (KD) when the current model distribution is close to the target distribution, while exhibiting a disadvantage when the two distributions are far apart. Furthermore, when the target distribution itself depends on the model being optimized, we show that the accumulation of estimation variance can induce a deterministic degradation of the target distribution. These results provide a theoretical explanation, at least in part, for the long-term behavior of existing Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms. With this intuition we further designed Conditional KL (CKL) regularization for mitigating the degradation of the target distribution. CKL can effectively preserve mode diversity while relaxing the constraint imposed by classical KL regularization on reward improvements. We believe this theoretical perspective can bring some new understanding of language model training algorithms and provide useful guidance for future research.

papers.title: ProtAgent: Post-Training Compact Protein Tool Agents with Interaction-Level Credit Assignment
papers.abstract: Protein annotation agents must choose suitable bioinformatics tools, interpret their outputs, and use the resulting evidence in the final answer. Most existing systems rely on frontier-scale models. We ask whether a compact model can instead learn this behavior through post-training with real tool interaction. We present ProtAgent, a two-stage pipeline that uses supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the tool interface and standard on-policy REINFORCE to improve the interaction policy. Intermediate tool calls receive action rewards, and the final response receives a terminal answer reward. Step-level returns assign these rewards to the responses that produced them and to preceding actions. The episode-level baseline instead assigns one episode return to every action. On a fixed closed-loop protocol with real bioinformatics tools, ProtAgent-8B achieves 61.00% success under the annotation-coverage metric, compared with 41.60% for DeepSeek-V3.2-Thinking 671B and 60.80% for the strongest evaluated frontier system. In the three-seed comparison, mean success is 42.70% with episode-level returns and 61.40% with step-level returns under identity return normalization; the corresponding group-relative results are 36.50% and 58.20%. The metric measures recovery of reference annotations under this protocol; it does not by itself establish biological correctness or complete evidence grounding.

papers.title: A Bestiary of Brownian Processes: A Field Guide to Boundary Conditions and Conditioning
papers.abstract: The covariance of Brownian motion is the Green kernel of the one-dimensional Laplacian with a pinned left endpoint and a free right endpoint. This correspondence between Green's functions for the Laplacian on an interval and Brownian covariance functions turns out to be a general phenomenon. We use this correspondence to organize Brownian-derived Gaussian processes by three operations: choosing a self-adjoint realization, recentering a path, and conditioning a fixed law. Local Robin and selected nonlocal boundary conditions yield a catalogue of twelve processes with closed-form kernels, Brownian-path constructions, spectra and traces. The periodic and Neumann-Neumann realizations annihilate the constants; projecting the source and imposing zero time average selects the corresponding covariance pseudoinverses. Recentering and conditioning can both give a Brownian path zero time average, but the resulting laws differ: a constraint alone does not specify a process. A rank-one conditioning identity gives a scale-invariant criterion for the covariance effect of a shrinking family of observations. For Brownian finite differences of any fixed positive order, the covariance effect vanishes uniformly as the spacing tends to zero. For $m$-fold integrated Brownian motion, derivative constraints of orders $1,\ldots,m$ remain detectable at interior times. For simulation, we identify which grid constructions are exact and which are approximate.

papers.title: A Rowhammer attack on Fil-C's software capabilities
papers.abstract: Rowhammer is a hardware vulnerability in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) in which repeated accesses to one or more aggressor rows can induce bit-flips in nearby victim rows. This phenomenon violates a core assumption of conventional programming language semantics: that reading from or writing to one memory location does not modify others. Despite the security importance of this phenomenon, there is no widely established formal framework connecting Rowhammer faults with program behaviour. This makes it difficult to reason rigorously about the efficacy of proposed Rowhammer defences and the program-level guarantees they provide. To address this gap, we present a probabilistic small-step operational semantics for an idealised imperative language subject to Rowhammer-style faults. The semantics is high-level in that it abstracts from DRAM internals and semiconductor physics. A general probabilistic fault model parameterises the semantics, representing Rowhammer-style faults by assigning probabilities to bit-flips during read or write operations within a specified victim region. The resulting distributions are propagated through programs using the standard monadic structure of probabilistic computation. As a case study, we formalise physical separation, a well-known defence that places program variables sufficiently far apart in physical memory that an access to one variable cannot disturb another. We prove a distribution-independent semantic collapse theorem: for every finite execution, including prefixes of terminating and non-terminating executions, the protected projection of the probabilistic Rowhammer semantics is the Dirac distribution of the corresponding Rowhammer-free execution. Furthermore, we develop an observation-parametric account of secure information flow.

papers.title: Uniform asymptotics and the Weil--Petersson constant
papers.abstract: In their celebrated work on the large-genus asymptotic expansion of Weil--Petersson volumes, Mirzakhani and Zograf left open the question of whether the Weil--Petersson constant satisfies $C_{\mathrm{WP}}=π^{-1/2}$. For each fixed number $n\geq2$ of marked points, we normalize the cusp coefficients using the action integral and the derivative at its first positive zero. We prove that the logarithmic derivatives of these normalized coefficients with respect to the family parameter are $O_n(g^{-1})$, uniformly along the family. The proof combines the descendant recursion, positivity, the dilaton equation, KdV, and coefficient asymptotics for the Painlevé I equation.

papers.title: Computer Vision Navigation for an Autonomous Vehicle Model Using Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This work aims to assess the capabilities of the reinforcement learning algorithm, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), in developing a policy capable of controlling the speed and steering angle of a vehicle model to navigate within simulated road lines. The control system's input is a camera, and its outputs are the rotational speed of the rear wheels and the steering angle of the front wheels, controlling the vehicle's speed and direction, respectively. The algorithm is trained and tested in a simulated environment, where it receives image frames from the vehicle's camera, processes them through a feature extraction algorithm, and feeds them into the policy. For each frame, the policy outputs speed and direction commands for the vehicle. The policy is iteratively updated to enhance its performance. The reinforcement learning algorithm successfully generates a policy capable of navigating the vehicle in a simplified environment. Potential improvements are suggested to enhance the system's robustness in more complex scenarios. Creating a simulation environment suitable for testing an advanced reinforcement learning algorithm is a complex task. This project offers a framework for other developers to test different approaches and algorithms. The tested algorithm, PPO, uses proximity intervals - an innovative approach in reinforcement learning. In some scenarios, the algorithm achieved better performance than predecessor algorithms, which are typically harder to implement and require tuning more hyperparameters.

history_evidence.official_title: Computer Vision Navigation for an Autonomous Vehicle Model Using Reinforcement Learning
history_evidence.official_abstract: This work aims to assess the capabilities of the reinforcement learning algorithm, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), in developing a policy capable of controlling the speed and steering angle of a vehicle model to navigate within simulated road lines. The control system's input is a camera, and its outputs are the rotational speed of the rear wheels and the steering angle of the front wheels, controlling the vehicle's speed and direction, respectively. The algorithm is trained and tested in a simulated environment, where it receives image frames from the vehicle's camera, processes them through a feature extraction algorithm, and feeds them into the policy. For each frame, the policy outputs speed and direction commands for the vehicle. The policy is iteratively updated to enhance its performance. The reinforcement learning algorithm successfully generates a policy capable of navigating the vehicle in a simplified environment. Potential improvements are suggested to enhance the system's robustness in more complex scenarios. Creating a simulation environment suitable for testing an advanced reinforcement learning algorithm is a complex task. This project offers a framework for other developers to test different approaches and algorithms. The tested algorithm, PPO, uses proximity intervals - an innovative approach in reinforcement learning. In some scenarios, the algorithm achieved better performance than predecessor algorithms, which are typically harder to implement and require tuning more hyperparameters.

papers.title: All the Facts, Still the Wrong Answer: Integration Gaps in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal reasoning requires models to combine multiple pieces of evidence into decisions that satisfy all relevant constraints. Evaluations centered on final-answer accuracy leave unclear whether failures arise from reading individual facts or using them together. We study this question through the multi-evidence integration gap, linking local fact recovery to global decision validity on controlled subset-selection and path-finding tasks. Our evaluation combines conditional performance given correct local answers with same-grid local queries, text-oracle inputs, retrieval controls, and constraint ablations. We further examine hidden-state probes and activation replacement across network depth, token positions, and model families. Across the evaluated models, accurate local recovery coexists with substantial global failure. For example, Gemma-3-27B recovers all evaluated isolated item facts correctly but achieves only 19.75% global validity on eight-item visual instances. Probes decode information about solution membership from global-prompt states, while corresponding clean-state replacement recovers failed decisions over model-dependent depth ranges. These findings show that recovering facts and representing solution-related information are insufficient for reliable joint decisions. They motivate evaluations and model improvements that explicitly target how available evidence is combined, alongside advances in perception and model scale.

papers.title: RoleHear: Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Role-Attributed Streaming Speech Recognition
papers.abstract: Streaming automatic speech recognition transcribes at low latency but produces an unattributed word stream, while real-time applications such as customer-service analytics need each word tied to a speaker role. Role attribution is usually a separate stage, either an offline or streaming speaker-diarization model aligned to the words or a text-based large language model applied to the transcript, and role labels for training are scarce. We present RoleHear, a semi-supervised pipeline that makes a single cache-aware streaming transducer emit roles inline through lightweight in-vocabulary role tokens: a fast turn-boundary marker followed by a per-role token a few words later. An offline transducer teacher, fine-tuned into a role-attributed recognizer, relabels unlabeled audio, and a multimodal large language model supplies silver role labels where gold annotations are unavailable. The streaming student is fine-tuned on the mixture in a single pass. Across customer-service calls with gold roles and earnings calls with silver roles, RoleHear attributes roles accurately while preserving transcription quality and narrowing the gap to the offline teacher.

papers.title: On the stability of second-order methods for DDEs and PDDEs
papers.abstract: In this paper, a one-parameter family of second-order implicit--explicit (IMEX) multistep methods is studied for delay differential equations (DDEs). The analysis is based on the matrix problem $y'(t)=A y(t) + B y(t-τ(t))$, where $A$ is Hermitian negative definite but $B$ is any matrix. For constant, grid-aligned delays, a field-of-values argument yields unconditional stability whenever a suitable generalized field of values $F_p(A,B)$ is contained in the open unit disk. For a constant non-grid-aligned delay, we show that quadratic interpolation does not reduce the corresponding stability disk. For genuinely variable delays, the method is formulated as a nonautonomous augmented system, and product-level sufficient conditions are obtained from a common quadratic Lyapunov inequality and from a quantitative slow-variation hypothesis. The approach developed herein is illustrated through several examples in which the discussed theory is applied not only to DDEs, but also to semidiscrete parabolic problems given by partial delay differential equations with a diffusion term.

papers.title: Wave-branch classification of ideal MHD discontinuities in Q-variables
papers.abstract: The $Q$-variable formalism combines velocity and magnetic field into branches aligned with a selected MHD wave. For homogeneous ideal MHD, appropriate choices of the branch parameter $α$ correspond to the fast, Alfvén, and slow characteristic families, with the background variables $\boldsymbol{Q}_0^{\pm}$ representing the propagation direction and speed of the corresponding characteristics. In structured plasmas, $α$ may instead be selected from the dispersion relation of a global mode such as a kink wave. Recent work reformulated the ideal-MHD Rankine-Hugoniot conditions in $Q$-variables and established their exact equivalence with the classical conservative jump conditions. Here, we apply this formulation to the standard ideal-MHD discontinuity catalogue. We determine how the two discontinuity-frame branches $\boldsymbol{Q}^{\prime+}$ and $\boldsymbol{Q}^{\prime-}$, their sums, and their $α$-normalised differences are constrained across contact, tangential, and rotational discontinuities and across the principal shock families. Material interfaces are distinguished by their normal branch content, rotational discontinuities by an Alfvénic tangential relation, and fast, slow, and intermediate shocks by the magnitude or orientation of the $α$-normalised tangential branch difference. Perpendicular, parallel, switch-on, and switch-off shocks appear as geometrical or limiting cases. The resulting classification expresses the classical discontinuity conditions in a wave-aligned form and, through the characteristic interpretation of $\boldsymbol{Q}_0^{\pm}$, shows how ideal-MHD discontinuities constrain changes in characteristic propagation direction and speed across the interface. It therefore establishes the background interface structure required for subsequent studies of reflection, transmission, coupling, and mode conversion.

papers.title: One Scan is Enough: Demonstration-Free Adaptation for Language-Guided Navigation
papers.abstract: Deploying a language - guided navigation policy in a new building usually means watching it fail. Public-benchmark VLAs degrade scene by scene as layout, appearance, and language drift, and the standard fix of teleoperating fresh trajectories on site does not scale. We replace human demonstration with a single brief iPhone scan. Scan2Instruction compiles that scan into a complete training environment, automatically synthesizing executable navigation episodes with grounded instructions. PRPT-KS then adapts the policy through a closed-form Pareto utility read directly off the reconstructed scene, with no learned critic and no human labels. Across five real environments, the two designs together drive our RealNav to an 85% real-robot success rate, compared with 49% for a RealNav baseline post-trained on human demonstrations, and still achieve 82% in unscanned regions of the same buildings, compared with 41% for the same baseline. Our work turns demonstration-free scene adaptation for language - guided navigation from an aspiration into a working reality.

papers.title: Variational Structure of Energy-Balance Climate Models with Heterogeneous Insolation
papers.abstract: We analyse stationary Sellers-type energy-balance climate models with heterogeneous insolation $Q_\varepsilon = Q_*+\varepsilon Q_1$, both on the interval $(-1,1)$ with degenerate diffusion $κ(x)=1-x^2$ and on $\mathbb{S}^2$ with uniformly elliptic diffusion. Assuming that the homogeneous model corresponding to $\varepsilon = 0$ admits three constant equilibria $θ_S <θ_M < θ_W$ satisfying suitable non-degeneracy and spectral conditions, we prove that, for sufficiently small $\vert \varepsilon \vert $, these equilibria continue to three stationary branches $ u_S^\varepsilon$, $u_M^\varepsilon$, and $u_W^\varepsilon$. The cold and warm branches, $u_S^\varepsilon$ and $u_W^\varepsilon$ respectively, are strict local minimisers of the associated energy functional, while the intermediate branch $u_M^\varepsilon$ is non-degenerate and has Morse index one. We further establish the Palais-Smale condition and obtain a mountain-pass critical point $u^\varepsilon_{MP}$ at the minimax level between the two local minima. Under an additional isolation assumption for the homogeneous problem at the minimax level, this critical point coincides with $u_M^\varepsilon$. Lastly, a Legendre-Galerkin discretisation of the one-dimensional model numerically illustrates the three stationary branches, their discrete Morse indices, and the corresponding energy landscape.

papers.title: Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Simulation of molecular vibrations is emerging as a promising application of quantum computing in quantum chemistry. In this work, we develop new strategies for block-encoding the second-quantized $n$-mode representation of the vibrational Hamiltonian, whose algebraic structure closely parallels that of the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. We derive linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) representations of this Hamiltonian based on Pauli decomposition and tensor hypercontraction (THC) and construct efficient circuits for the corresponding block encodings. We also extend the Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) technique to vibrational Hamiltonians, yielding a lower LCU 1-norm and, consequently, a lower overall circuit cost. For the molecules considered here, BLISS-THC reduces the Toffoli cost of quantum phase estimation by more than two orders of magnitude relative to existing block-encoding approaches. In comparison with recent Trotter-based methods, it shows up to a ninefold reduction in the T-gate count, with the relative savings tending to increase with system size. Asymptotically, and up to polylogarithmic factors, both the Pauli and THC LCUs trade additional ancillas for a quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modes, while THC provides an additional quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modals. These results highlight the importance of Hamiltonian factorizations and Toffoli-qubit tradeoffs for reducing the computational cost of quantum simulations of molecular vibrations.

papers.title: ProMo3D: Probing Motion Cues in Frozen 3D Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models have recently reshaped multi-view reconstruction, yet dynamic 4D understanding still often relies on large-scale motion supervision or hand-crafted, architecture-specific heuristics. We ask whether frozen 3D foundation model tokens already encode motion-relevant information that can be exposed by lightweight readout functions, rather than re-learning motion-specific features with high-capacity decoders. Through probing on three representative backbones, we find that static--dynamic separation is decodable from frozen token representations. Our rank-restricted and spectral analyses on $π^3$X reveal that the recovered motion cues are concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this, we propose Probing-based Motion Distillation (PMD), which converts pairwise motion-state compatibility scores against a fixed anchor token into dense motion masks. Trained on only 160 YouTube-VOS videos using a single 16 GB GPU, PMD transfers zero-shot to DAVIS, SegTrackv2, and FBMS-59 without target-benchmark fine-tuning. With multi-view pretrained geometric backbones, PMD outperforms training-free heuristics and approaches substantially heavier supervised and self-supervised methods, suggesting that motion decoding from frozen 3D foundation models can be lightweight and data-efficient.

papers.title: Fermiophobic Z' Bosons in 3-4-1 Models: Classification and Collider Constraints
papers.abstract: We investigate the fermion spectra and collider phenomenology of models based on the \(SU(3)_C \otimes SU(4)_L \otimes U(1)_X\) gauge symmetry, focusing on two realizations of the electric charge operator characterized by \(b=c=1\) and \(b=1,\ c=-2\). For each configuration, we classify anomaly-free fermion sets and identify five minimal spectra with at least three SM-like quark and lepton families for each configuration, distinguishing algebraically irreducible structures from reducible spectra that remain minimal under the three-family requirement. We derive the chiral couplings of the additional neutral gauge boson \(Z'\) to Standard Model fermions and show that distinct anomaly-free fermion spectra can lead to identical low-energy neutral-current interactions. We then investigate the corresponding collider constraints using the ATLAS dilepton resonance search at \(\sqrt{s}=13\) TeV with an integrated luminosity of \(139\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}\), assuming negligible \(Z-Z'\) mixing and kinematically inaccessible exotic fermions. A particularly interesting result emerges for the \(b=c=1\) configuration, where all \(Z'\) couplings to Standard Model fermions are proportional to \(\sinψ\), with \(ψ\) denoting the additional neutral gauge-boson mixing angle. Consequently, these couplings vanish simultaneously at \(ψ=nπ\), giving rise to a fermiophobic limit in which conventional Drell-Yan dilepton constraints disappear. In contrast, the \(b=1,\ c=-2\) configuration does not exhibit a universal fermiophobic limit. Our results demonstrate that collider constraints on additional neutral gauge bosons depend sensitively on the fermion embeddings and neutral gauge-boson mixing structure, and suggest the possibility of comparatively light \(Z'\) bosons in suitable realizations of extended electroweak gauge theories.

papers.title: RoboWorM: Evaluating Movement Realism, Consistency and Acceleration Affects in Embodied Video World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models (VWMs) are rapidly emerging as scalable neural simulators for robotic manipulation. However, most benchmarks only evaluate them as open-world video generators, using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that lack strict 3D spatial and kinematic reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboWorM, a comprehensive, deployment-aware benchmark that leverages known hardware priors such as robot kinematic trees and fixed camera configurations, to systematically examine structural and spatiotemporal fidelity. RoboWorM curates 1,605 episodes across single-arm, bimanual, and humanoid morphologies, spanning both Markovian and long-horizon non-Markovian tasks under single- and multi-view setups. To explicitly measure physical consistency, we propose two deterministic, VLM-free metrics: KIVA for intra-view kinematic stability, and RIGIS for multi-view geometric consistency. By exploiting intrinsic robotic invariants, KIVA improves hallucination detection alignment with human annotations by 25.8% relative to the strongest frontier VLMs, while RIGIS achieves a 130% higher Spearman correlation with human preferences. Furthermore, since real-world deployment requires low inference latency, we utilize RoboWorM to conduct the first large-scale audit of the quality-efficiency trade-off. Evaluating 9 state-of-the-art acceleration techniques across 3 leading world models (over 29,000 generated rollouts), we demonstrate how these acceleration methods can retain superficial visual quality while silently compromising deployment-critical physical constraints. history_evidence.official_title: RoboWorM: Evaluating Movement Realism, Consistency and Acceleration Affects in Embodied Video World Models
history_evidence.official_abstract: Video world models (VWMs) are rapidly emerging as scalable neural simulators for robotic manipulation. Furthermore, since real-world deployment requires low inference latency, we utilize RoboWorM to conduct the first large-scale audit of the quality-efficiency trade-off. Evaluating 9 state-of-the-art acceleration techniques across 3 leading world models (over 29,000 generated rollouts), we demonstrate how these acceleration methods can retain superficial visual quality while silently compromising deployment-critical physical constraints. Using our metrics, we achieve 2.3$\times$ maximum inference speed-up with minimal quality loss.

papers.title: Emergent parafermions with tunable localization in a quantum circuit network
papers.abstract: \noindent Quantum circuit simulators with hybrid metal-semiconductor dots provide a versatile platform to realize Kondo anyons. These arise at critical points driven by frustrated Kondo screening of dot charge degrees of freedom and have been demonstrated experimentally in linear circuits of one or two dots. Here we study a triangular triple dot device, where geometric frustration gives rise to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_3$ parafermion shared among the three dots. We show that the parafermion can be tunably relocated to any pair of dots by applying gate voltages, and is supported in both the weak-tunneling `Kondo limit' and the strong transmission `quasiballistic' regime. The critical states survive strong coupling to external leads and other dots, establishing the basis for a scalable and reconfigurable network architecture in which non-Abelian excitations can be realized and manipulated.

papers.title: Optimal Control of the 2D Boussinesq Equations with Finite Codimension Constraints
papers.abstract: We study an optimal control problem (OCP) governed by the two-dimensional (2D) Boussinesq equations, where the right-hand sides of the velocity and temperature equations are projected onto the corresponding tangent spaces of the manifolds $\mathcal{M}_1:=\{y\in\mathbb{H}:\|y\|_{\mathbb{H}}=1\}$ and $\mathcal{M}_2:=\{θ\in H:\|θ\|_H=1\}$, respectively. The resulting evolution is subject to finite-codimensional constraints, under which the state $(y,θ)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}:=\mathcal{M}_1\times\mathcal{M}_2$ throughout the time interval. A Faedo--Galerkin construction provides a unique, global, strong solution to the constrained Boussinesq system for external controls $\mathfrak{H}\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb{H})$, along with uniform energy bounds. In addition, we establish the existence of an optimal triplet $(y^*,θ^*,\mathfrak{H}^*)$ that minimizes the quadratic cost subject to the constrained Boussinesq system. Necessary conditions of the first order are obtained through a coupled state--adjoint--control system. The optimal state $(y^*,θ^*)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}$, while the optimal control lies in the tangent space: $\mathfrak{H}^*(t)\in T_{y^*(t)}\mathcal{M}_1$, for all $t\in[0,T]$. We also show that the map $\mathfrak{H}\mapsto(y_{\mathfrak{H}},θ_{\mathfrak{H}})$ in $(C([0,T];\mathbb{H})\cap L^2(0,T;\mathbb{V}))\times(C([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;V))$ is Fréchet differentiable. The linearized state is the unique weak solution to the constrained linearized Boussinesq system and satisfies the necessary tangency condition. Hence, the well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions are established for the Boussinesq system under nonlinear manifold constraints.

papers.title: Sliding Networks: A Family of Residual Structures Preserving Feature Learning and Feature Diversity
papers.abstract: Deep learning models tend to perform best at large widths and depths. The growing interest in scaling laws, especially in the language modeling domain, has motivated procedures for scaling up network widths and depths in order to preserve stability and computational efficiency of training dynamics. Existing depth-scaling approaches force a choice between retaining locally maximal \emph{feature learning} and preserving a form of \emph{feature diversity} in the residual stream arising from random differences between channels. We examine a \textit{joint scaling recipe} that preserves both. With residual width $N_\flat$, hidden width $N_\sharp$, and depth $L$, the key quantity is, by default, the limiting ratio $N_\flat/(N_\sharp L)\toα$, while correlated initialization (Half Copy) can partially relax the resulting shape constraints. Theory and residual-MLP experiments support convergence at fixed positive $α$ to an SDE limit with locally maximal feature learning. Hidden computations can then be redistributed between width and depth while preserving this limit, like turning melody into harmony and back. Language-model experiments nevertheless show performance differences under regrouping at fixed parameter count. These results distinguish approximating a limit (ODE or SDE) from scaling for better performance.

papers.title: Real-Time Recurrent Qubit-State Discrimination on a Heterogeneous AI-Engine-FPGA Accelerator
papers.abstract: Qubit readout, or qubit state discrimination, remains one of the slowest and most error-prone operations in superconducting quantum processors, making fast, accurate, and hardware-efficient classification essential for scalable quantum computing. Conventional discriminators integrate the I/Q record into a single point, discarding evidence a relaxing qubit leaves behind; full-resolution feed-forward classifiers recover it but are too costly to deploy under this constraint. Recurrent classifiers retain full resolution far more cheaply, but their loop-carried hidden state cannot fit a single AI Engine (AIE) tile's register capacity and spills to data memory, adding latency that grows with sequence length. We present a hardware-aware LSTM accelerator for an AMD Versal device that resolves this by partitioning at the dependency boundary - independent input projections on the AIE array, the loop-carried update in programmable logic (PL) - keeping pace with a 64 ns input cadence under a 1,000 ns budget. On the qubit affected by mid-readout state transitions, our design matches a full-resolution feed-forward network's accuracy (96.59% vs. 96.37%) using 403x fewer parameters and roughly 103x fewer DSPs while cutting relative error by 68.2% over GMM, 43.6% over QubiCML, and 16.82% over MF-NN. Using 4 out of 400 AIE tiles and 17 DSP58, it needs 2.2-8.2x fewer DSP58 blocks than QubiCML and MF-NN, and the AIE-PL partition cuts exposed tail latency by 60.3% versus a pure-AIE mapping and DSP58 usage 31.1x versus an all-PL implementation. Across eight qubits, a compact variant reaches 96.78% mean accuracy, the strongest hardware-deployed operating point. Temporal resolution and recurrent-state placement must then be treated jointly when designing low-latency quantum readout accelerators.

papers.title: AdaDexTrack: Dynamic Modulation for Adaptive and Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation Tracking
papers.abstract: Language is a natural way to command robots, but converting a single instruction into a long-horizon, contact-rich hand-object interaction remains challenging: synthesized references are noisy, human-to-robot retargeting introduces embodiment bias, and fixed-reference tracking lets small errors snowball. We address this with AdaDexTrack, a modulator-in-the-loop framework for language-conditioned manipulation tracking. A distilled generalist tracker serves as the skill carrier, while a tightly aligned modulator performs three feedback corrections: reference modulation (continual adjustment of what to track), object-latent modulation (online adaptation of the object representation to recruit suitable skills), and positional-target modulation (small state-dependent refinements for execution). The tracker is learned via large-scale specialist to generalist distillation on a corpus of language-conditioned hand-object trajectories; the modulator is trained with RL under the same task objective, ensuring tight coupling. Across large-scale evaluations, AdaDexTrack consistently outperforms prior SOTA on unseen-trajectory and unseen-object sets in both average tracking error and success rate, demonstrating robustness and generalization. We further show zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on real hardware, where adding the modulator yields substantial gains over a tracker-only variant. AdaDexTrack reframes language-conditioned dexterous manipulation as modulated tracking, replacing the open-loop, fixed-reference tracking with in-loop modulation that adjusts the reference, object latent, and positional target, yielding drift-resistant execution from noisy text references.

papers.title: RoboLongR: Causally Consistent Rewards Teach Robots to Progressively Master Long-Horizon Manipulation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation requires actions whose validity depends on earlier interactions, yet visual progress can conceal missing task prerequisites. We propose RoboLongR, an offline-to-online framework that learns history-dependent rewards to guide policy adaptation to new tasks. Its central objective is causal consistency: aligning rewarded progress with prerequisites supported by execution history. Stage-shuffle supervision encourages execution-order sensitivity, recurrent memory preserves evidence of earlier interactions, and two-round training refines trajectory segments using predicted progress. The resulting rewards guide stage-conditioned policy refinement from behavior cloning to online reinforcement learning. Sparse terminal feedback connects policy experience to reward learning by triggering correction for repeated high-scoring failures. Pretrained on demonstrations from 88 RLBench tasks and Open-X data, RoboLongR achieves 31.8% average success on 18 long-horizon tasks excluded from reward pretraining, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 9.2 percentage points. Across four real-robot tasks, it achieves 57.5% success, a 32.5-percentage-point improvement over the comparison method. Reward-level controls probe sensitivity to synthetic order perturbations, while ablations examine the contributions of individual components to policy improvement.

papers.title: Efficiency--Complexity Tradeoff and Constrained Percolation
papers.abstract: We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions. Our main result concerns the limiting cost parameterized by path-family entropy. Using techniques from analytic combinatorics in several variables (ACSV), we establish its almost-sure existence and joint continuity in entropy and direction for nested families satisfying additional generating-function conditions, on the corresponding entropy range. Path-count asymptotics supply the change of parameter linking this cost to the constraint-parameterized cost. Two planar examples constrain the number of turns or the number of East-runs of length at least two.

papers.title: RelateGS: Reliable Semantic and Relational Evidence for 3D Scene Understanding with Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Language-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has advanced language-driven 3D scene understanding by incorporating semantic and relational cues into reconstructed scenes. However, relation-aware grounding depends not only on representing such information, but also on whether the underlying scene-side evidence is reliable and sufficient. Multi-view semantic aggregation can incorporate weak observations, while object relations can remain under-observed along the available camera trajectory, leading to ambiguous evidence for target disambiguation. We present RelateGS, a structured language-aware Gaussian representation that selectively refines semantic and relational evidence for 3D visual grounding. RelateGS suppresses unreliable observations during semantic feature uplifting and consolidates multi-view object observations into a persistent 3D graph. The graph further identifies under-observed object relations and guides targeted re-querying of informative existing frames to complement their evidence. Experiments on Sr3D+ and Nr3D demonstrate competitive 3D grounding performance, improving the previous best by 7.9 and 1.7 percentage points at Acc@0.25, respectively.

papers.title: Using artificial delays for prescribed/fixed-time static output feedback control of linear systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the prescribed/fixed-time control problem for linear time-invariant systems with relative degree $r\geq 2$ using delayed time-varying static output feedback. In addition to controllability and observability, we assume that a truncated observability matrix is nonsingular. Within the act-and-wait control framework, two types of artificial delays are introduced into the output feedback: one to realize static output feedback and the other to achieve prescribed/fixed-time control. By constructing smooth periodic delayed output feedback controllers, we achieve prescribed-time input-to-state stability (ISS) with respect to matched disturbances and measurement noise. Next, we consider systems with measurement delays. Note that existing predictor methods are not applicable to static output feedback delay compensation. We propose delayed controllers that achieve fixed-time stability in the presence of large known slowly-varying delays (with delay derivatives less than one) and even in the presence of large unknown constant delays for systems with nilpotent matrices. Moreover, we present a design for the case of discrete-time periodic measurements with a small sampling period. When the system reduces to a chain of integrators, prescribed/fixed-time convergence can be achieved with arbitrarily large artificial delays introduced by static output feedback avoiding high gain and managing with large known slowly-varying or sawtooth delays (corresponding to discrete-time measurements) or unknown constant delays. In the case of unknown constant delays, this leads to a low-gain controller that may efficiently attenuate measurement noise. Numerical examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Well-posedness of the Burgers' equation on the half-line through the Cole-Hopf transformation
papers.abstract: We rigorously establish the well-posedness of the initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) for the Burgers' equation on the half-line for data in Sobolev-type spaces. The formal solution to this problem was previously derived via the Cole-Hopf transformation and the Fokas unified transform method under the assumption of smooth, Schwartz-class data. In this work, we prove the validity of this formal representation for initial data $u_0\in \tilde{H}^{s+1}_x (0,\infty)$ and boundary data $g_0 \in H_t^{{(2s+1)}/{4}}$ where $1/2<s<3/2$. Well-posedness is established under two complementary conditions: (1) sufficiently small initial and boundary data, and (2) non-positive boundary data of arbitrary size. The latter condition utilizes the strong minimum principle for the corresponding linear heat equation to ensure the global invertibility of the nonlinear Cole-Hopf map. papers.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
papers.abstract: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2πi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.

papers.title: Residual-Calibrated Multimodal Spatiotemporal Learning for Future Beam Prediction
papers.abstract: We propose a residual calibrated multimodal spatiotemporal framework for future beam prediction on DeepSense 6G Scenario 23. The framework integrates visual observations, location features, and historical beam labels to predict the beam label of the next dataset record. A pretrained Swin-Tiny encoder extracts features from four consecutive RGB frames. Bidirectional cross-attention integrates visual and two dimensional Unit 1 location representations, while a temporal Transformer incorporates historical beam label embeddings to model dependencies across the observation window. A supplementary offline residual head adjusts the frozen supervised logits using immediate correctness rewards and an auxiliary classification loss. A fixed probability mixture of the supervised and residual outputs is selected using validation accuracy. From 11,387 aligned records, we construct 11,255 temporal windows and partition them by capture run into 7,854 training, 1,905 validation, and 1,496 test samples. The supervised predictor achieves Top-1, Top-2, Top-3, and Top-5 test accuracies of 62.83%, 74.80%, 79.75%, and 81.08%, respectively. The residual predictor achieves corresponding accuracies of 61.76%, 75.07%, 79.41%, and 81.02%. Residual adjustment increases Top-2 accuracy by 0.27 percentage points, while the supervised predictor retains higher Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 accuracies. The validation-selected mixture coincides with the residual predictor. The proposed framework combines cross-modal sensing features with explicit beam-history conditioning and a separately trained residual adjustment stage for one-record-ahead beam prediction. Initial evaluation on held-out capture runs characterizes the candidate-ranking performance of both prediction stages and favors the supervised variant for Top-1 selection. These findings motivate further study of historical conditioning and residual refinement.

papers.title: WMEval: Evaluating Interactive World Models Grounded on Physical Simulations
papers.abstract: Interactive world models hold immense potential for high-stakes applications in robotics, game engines, and immersive digital twins, yet existing benchmarks primarily focus on perceptual similarity rather than the physical-causal coherence essential for real-world utility. We introduce WMEval, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates interactive world models against Unity-based physical simulations. By leveraging Unity as a high-fidelity ground-truth oracle, we shift evaluation beyond perceptual visual assessment toward the objective state-based verification required for downstream applications. Spanning 9 diverse scenes, WMEval assesses action controllability, scene and character consistency, prompt adherence, kinematics, fluid mechanics, physical causality, and lighting. By executing matched action sequences in both the simulator and the world model, WMEval enables evaluation at both the perceptual level and the physical-causal level, using simulator-derived states as reference. Experiments on state-of-the-art models reveal significant room for improvement in dimensions that remain hidden by standard perceptual metrics but are vital for real-world deployments. Our code is available at: https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/WMEval.

papers.title: Fear Doesn't Go Viral, It Lingers: Spread, Affect, and Discourse of Food-Fear Content on TikTok
papers.abstract: TikTok has become a primary channel for nutrition information, and alongside evidence-based content, it hosts a growing stream of \emph{fear-based} wellness messaging that frames ordinary foods as ``toxic,'' ``poison,'' or things to ``never eat.'' Prior work has extensively studied political and public-health misinformation and audited the accuracy of health videos, but to the best of our knowledge, no work has examined how everyday food-fear content spreads and how audiences respond to it. To investigate this, we collected 97,234 TikTok food and nutrition videos, labeled them \textit{Fear} or \textit{Non-Fear} with a zero-shot multimodal classifier built on Gemini~3 Flash that is validated against human consensus (Cohen's $κ=0.81$), and analyzed more than 1.1M comments and 272K parent-reply pairs. Contrary to the intuition that fear ``goes viral,'' fear videos reach fewer people than non-fear videos. Their distinctive signature lies in dynamics: they are shared more per view (1.7--2.1$\times$ after controls) and their discussion persists longer (comment half-life 1.62$\times$ after controls). These shifts are modest in size but hold after controlling for reach. Comments on fear videos are more negative, angrier, and more disgusted, yet negativity is \emph{not} more self-reinforcing: negative comments draw negative replies at the same rate as in non-fear threads, while positive comments are far less likely to stay positive. Fear threads are contested rather than one-sided, with both more corrective and more alarm-amplifying replies. Fear discourse concentrates in frames about industrial ingredients, contaminants, and institutional distrust, and its repertoire of frames widens over 2020--2026. Our results argue for persistence-based rather than virality-based signals when platforms seek harmful health content.

papers.title: Ellipsoid Separation in Data-Dependent Time via Infimal Displacement Vectors
papers.abstract: The infimal displacement vector of the nonexpansive operator underlying the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm (PDHG) is known to encode useful information for infeasible optimization problems. In particular, for the ellipsoid separation problem (ESP), where the goal is to find a separating hyperplane between two collections of ellipsoids, the infimal displacement vector corresponding to an infeasible second-order cone program (SOCP) encodes a separating hyperplane. We show FISTA computes a sequence of approximations to the dual component of the infimal displacement vector and establish that a solution to the ESP can be obtained in $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-2})$ iterations. Here $δ_{\mathcal{A}}$ denotes the distance between the convex hulls of the two ellipsoid collections.

papers.title: Real-Time Human Trajectory Prediction from RGB-D for Mobile Robots Using Bi-Mamba
papers.abstract: Predicting the short-term future trajectory of a person from RGB-D cameras is a key capability for mobile robots navigating in dynamic and human populated environment. The key challenge to deploying learned predictors on real robots is the train-deploy pipeline gap. Training data are often prepared with an idealized, smoothed ground truth, whereas at inference, the model is fed noisy estimates from pose detectors and depth sensors. The model is therefore evaluated on an input distribution it never encountered during training. Most existing models rely on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or transformers, which either struggle to capture short-term temporal dependencies or suffer from computational cost. We present TrajMamba, a lightweight, bidirectional state space model for short-term human trajectory prediction using an RGB-D camera. The model uses a single shared processing path for both training and deployment, aligning human pose extraction, depth back projection, and smoothing processes. It encodes a short window of persons's hip center velocities with stacked bidirectional Mamba blocks and decodes future velocities with a GRU head. On the ETH/UCY benchmark, TrajMamba reaches an average ADE of 0.29 m FDE of 0.51 m. With 262K parameters, it runs in real time on modest hardware and is deployed on a TIAGo robot with an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin.

papers.title: TurboWAM: Learning What Matters for Fast World Action Models
papers.abstract: World action models have demonstrated promising performance in robot policy learning, yet their high inference latency remains a critical bottleneck for real-world deployment. Recent approaches have sought to improve inference efficiency by reducing test-time future-frame imagination or accelerating action prediction. However, these methods often leverage representations from all video world model layers without explicitly considering their varying relevance to action prediction, leading to redundant computation and suboptimal representation utilization. In this work, we propose TurboWAM, a fast world action model that efficiently aggregates structured world representations conditioned on action predictions. Specifically, TurboWAM introduces a structured world representation aggregation module that adaptively fuses representations from different world model layers according to their relevance to the evolving action denoising state. Furthermore, TurboWAM employs a structured action supervision mechanism that adaptively modulates gradients from action supervision across different world model layers during backward propagation, facilitating world representation learning. During inference, by reducing the number of world model layers executed and caching relevant representations across action denoising steps, TurboWAM substantially reduces computational overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that TurboWAM achieves low inference latency while maintaining competitive task success rates compared with state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of transonic steady nozzle flows
papers.abstract: In the present article, we prove the nonlinear asymptotic stability of stationary solutions to the quasi-one-dimensional barotropic Euler equations in a finite-length nozzle with variable cross-sectional area $A(x)$. We consider all stationary flow configurations arising from subsonic inflow: flows that remain subsonic throughout the nozzle, flows that pass continuously through a sonic state and remain supersonic up to the exit, and flows that subsequently return to the subsonic regime through a stationary shock. We prove that all these stationary solutions are asymptotically stable with respect to sufficiently small perturbations. No smallness restrictions are imposed on the mass flux, the magnitude of $A_x$, or the prescribed exit pressure, provided that the corresponding stationary solution exists. The only geometrical assumptions are that $A_{xx}>0$ at a smooth subsonic--supersonic transition, and $A_x>0$ at a stationary supersonic--subsonic shock. To the best of our knowledge, this gives the first nonlinear asymptotic stability result for a stationary flow passing smoothly from the subsonic to the supersonic regime in a finite-length nozzle. The principal analytical difficulty is the degeneracy of the characteristic structure at the sonic point. We overcome this difficulty by coupling energy structures adapted respectively to the subsonic and supersonic regimes. This coupling provides the dissipation needed to control the smooth sonic transition, and when combined with the dynamics of the shock, yields a unified nonlinear stability framework for smooth and discontinuous transonic nozzle flows.

papers.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. We introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark developed by 50+ domain experts to measure experience-driven improvement in realistic professional workflows. CLE comprises 120 human-authored tasks, each organised as a five-level ladder, yielding 600 levels spanning 89 professional roles across 12 occupational domains. Agents must pass each level to unlock the next, with later levels building on experience accumulated during earlier assignments. An evaluation agent assesses each submission against human-authored rubrics. We compare a single-submission setting with one that provides diagnostic feedback after failure and allows one revision. Across 17 harness-model configurations using frontier LLMs, feedback and revision yield a median completion gain of 5.3 percentage points. Yet the best-performing system clears only 47.7% of levels and completes all five levels in just 23.3% of tasks, highlighting the difficulty of sustained learning from experience for existing frontier LLMs. As such, the dataset can also be used to post-train LLMs to strengthen their continual learning capabilities.

papers.title: I Won't Know Until I Try: Interactive Information Gathering for Long-Horizon Manipulation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation often depends on object properties that cannot be reliably inferred from appearance alone. Physical interaction can reveal these properties, but it can also change the world in ways that invalidate subsequent actions. We present a task and motion planning (TAMP) framework that integrates task-directed interactive information-gathering with interleaved planning and execution. Building on PDDLStream, our framework plans optimistically with these interactive actions, verifies their outcomes during execution, and adapts the remaining plan by retaining still-applicable actions and replanning only the connections needed to continue execution. We evaluate the framework in simulation and on a real robot across tasks that require determining whether an object is movable, a pen has ink, a drawer can be opened, or a container is empty. These experiments demonstrate how interaction-driven state updates and recovery replanning support continued execution under uncertain outcomes and external disturbances.

papers.title: QECGBERT: A Scalable ECG Foundation Model Based on Self-Supervised Language Learning via VQ-VAE Waveform Tokenization
papers.abstract: AI foundation models play a pivotal role in advancing heart disease diagnosis from electrocardiogram (ECG) data, particularly for rare diseases where the lack of sufficient labeled data hinders supervised learning. However, most self-supervised learning methods treat ECGs as generic sequence or image data without exploiting underlying physiological structure. To address this limitation, we propose QECGBERT, a self-supervised ECG language model that explicitly encodes physiological semantics by tokenizing the P, QRS, T, and isoelectric background waveforms. Vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) tokenization is applied to each 12-lead ECG, with tokens enriched by continuous waveform features to preserve morphology lost during quantization without increasing sequence length. This design enables compact BERT masked language modeling with short sequences, improving scalability and reducing computational cost relative to long-sequence approaches. QECGBERT applies BERT pre-training to the MIMIC-IV dataset containing over 800,000 unlabeled ECG recordings, and fine-tuning on labeled PTB-XL, CPSC2018, and Chapman--Shaoxing--Ningbo datasets for evaluation. The results demonstrate that QECGBERT achieves comparable or superior performance to published benchmarks, offering a scalable, physiologically aware approach to ECG foundation modeling for cardiac diagnosis.

papers.title: Accuracy Is Not Enough: An Efficiency- and Statistics-Aware Benchmark of ResNet50 and Vision Transformer for Explainable Multi-Class Gastrointestinal Diseases Classification
papers.abstract: Automated classification of gastrointestinal (GI) findings in endoscopic images could support early diagnosis, but architectures are often chosen on accuracy alone. We present a controlled, reproducible benchmark of ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 for eight-class GI classification on the public Kvasir dataset (4,000 images), using a stratified split (400 test images) and stratified group 5-fold cross-validation over all images. In cross-validation, ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 reached 92.12% and 91.70% accuracy, and a two one-sided tests (TOST) procedure showed equivalence within a +/-3 percentage-point margin (difference +0.43 points, 90% CI -0.33 to +1.18; p < 0.001). The architectures differed mainly in cost: ResNet50 had 3.6 times fewer parameters and 4.3 times fewer operations, 2.5-fold lower single-image CPU latency (69 vs. 177 ms) and 3.8-fold higher GPU throughput. Cross-validated calibration was similar (expected calibration error 0.021 vs. 0.023). An edge-oriented transformer, MobileViT-S, was most accurate on the test split (95.5%) but lost 9.4 points when an acquisition artefact present in some classes (the ScopeGuide inset) was occluded, whereas ResNet50 was not significantly affected. On 500 unseen polyp images with expert masks, both models' Grad-CAM maps focused on the lesion (3.6 times chance). On a de-duplicated external subset of GastroVision (1,998 images), accuracy fell to 78-80% for all three models and differences between them remained small. Accuracy differences between architectures were thus small relative to the effects of shortcut learning and domain shift, whereas efficiency differences were large. An efficient CNN is a defensible default for resource-constrained screening, but no model is deployment-ready without local validation.

papers.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
papers.abstract: People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. Powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), egocentric AI assistants on wearable devices are bringing this dream within reach: they see what the user sees and give instructions for user's physical work when necessary. However, testing such assistance is challenging and usually requires real people. The expensive and rare real interaction data leaves a key question unanswered: Can today's MLLMs truly help people in physical world? To answer this question, we propose InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment for closed-loop interaction between human and AI assistant. Unlike existing robot-centric simulators, InteractiveWorld lets the assistant guide a human agent who observes the scene, understands instructions, and acts independently. It thus realistically simulates how AI assistant collaborates with human: the assistant instructs, the human acts, and the environment executes actions and updates what they see next. Building on it, we introduce InteractiveBench, the first dynamic benchmark for egocentric AI assistants, with 120 multi-turn tasks across six categories. In each task, the assistant guides the human in real time, and every instruction shapes the outcome, which is scored by verifiable, state-based rewards. Experiments with 12 frontier MLLMs show they are still far from reliable assistants. Even the strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, achieves at most 20% and 25% on long-horizon Guidance and Planning tasks, respectively. Overall, our work offers a verifiable platform and a rigorous evaluation set, laying a solid foundation for research on interactive MLLM assistants that truly help people in the physical world.

papers.title: Revisiting monodromy defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories
papers.abstract: Monodromy defects are fundamental objects in extended quantum systems with global symmetries. We study such defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories (CFT), which describe the universality class of $\text{O}(N)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. We develop an analytical theory of the defect phases, using both renormalization group and large $N$ expansion. In general (spacetime) dimensions $3\leq d<4$, multiple defect CFTs are identified, which are described by appropriate boundary conditions for the vector field near the defect. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.

papers.title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
papers.abstract: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. papers.title: Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Network for Single-Shot 3D Reconstruction from Fringe Patterns
papers.abstract: Deep learning facilitates rapid single shot three dimensional (3D) reconstruction using fringe projection profilometry (FPP), but recovering accurate surface height from a single high frequency fringe image remains challenging because both long-range spatial consistency and fine geometric details must be preserved. Convolutional networks are limited in modeling long range dependencies, whereas window-based Transformers establish global interactions only progressively with increasing depth. To address these limitations, a hybrid Mamba Transformer network is proposed for fringe to height regression. The network adopts a Swin based U shaped architecture and introduces visual state space modeling at the intermediate resolution encoder stage. An axial and dilated vision state space (ADVSS) block is further developed to enhance prescan feature encoding through local, dilated, and axial depthwise convolutions while retaining four directional selective scanning. This design combines linear complexity long range modeling with direction aware preservation of local fringe structures. Experiments on a publicly available FPP dataset show that the proposed method outperforms hNet, SwinConvUNet, UHRNet, and HiDNet in mean absolute error(MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), absolute relative error, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Using only one deformed fringe image, the proposed method achieves an RMSE of 0.548 mm and an SSIM of 0.9985, reducing RMSE by 65.2% and 59.6% relative to UHRNet and HiDNet, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining selective state space modeling with hierarchical window based attention for accurate single-shot FPP reconstruction.

papers.title: Sharp Quantitative Weighted Estimates for Lifted Maximal Operators with Applications
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish sharp quantitative weighted estimates for the lifted Hardy--Littlewood (resp Sobolev sharp) maximal operators $\{\mathcal M_θ\}_{θ\in(0,\infty)}$ (resp $\{\mathcal M_θ^\sharp\}_{θ\in(0,\infty)}$). Specifically, for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, $\upsilon\in A_p$, and $f\in L^p_\upsilon$, we prove that \begin{align*} \sup_{θ,λ\in(0,\infty)}λ^p \underset{\mathcal M_θ(f)(x,t)>λt^γ} {\int_{\mathbb R^n}\int_0^\infty} t^{γp-1}\,dt\,\upsilon(x)\,dx \lesssim [\upsilon]_{A_p}^{α_{p,γ}} \|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p, \end{align*} where $α_{p,γ}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $γ\in[-n,0)$ and $α_{p,γ}:=1$ otherwise and where the implicit positive constant depends only on $n$, $p$, and $γ$. For $\mathcal M_θ^\sharp$, the corresponding estimate holds with $\|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ replaced by $\|\nabla f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ for any $f\in\dot W^{1,p}_\upsilon$, and with $α_{p,γ}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $γ\in[-1,0)$ and $α_{p,γ}:=1$ otherwise. We show that, for an $A_1$ weight $\upsilon$, the weight constant in the above estimates becomes $[\upsilon]_{A_1}$ for the sharp ranges $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, or $p=1$ and $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus[-n,0]$ (resp. $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus[-1,0]$). We also prove that $α_{p,γ}$ is sharp, and we establish exact limiting formulae and characterize Muckenhoupt weights via weak-type bounds. As applications, we characterize the weighted Hardy(--Sobolev) space $H^1_\upsilon$ with $\upsilon\in A_1$ in terms of the truncated Riesz transforms with optimal range $γ\in \mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. More applications include the sharp weighted Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and the generalization to ball Banach function spaces.

papers.title: Observational evidence of the Gaia-Enceladus-Sausage merger's influence on the opposite side of the Galactic Center
papers.abstract: The Gaia-Enceladus-Sausage (GES) merger, which occurred approximately 8-11 Gyr ago, is a key event that shaped the Galactic inner halo. Its remnants have been studied extensively and are known to dominate the halo on the Near-side of the Galactic Center (GC), i.e. the side facing the Sun, but systematic evidence for whether the Far-side (the side beyond the GC as seen from the Sun) is similarly affected has been lacking. Using 14,056 red giant stars selected from SMSS DR4 and Gaia DR3 through stringent quality cuts, we compare the metallicity distributions, velocity-space distributions, velocity dispersions, anisotropy parameters, and action-space properties of the Near- and Far-sides. We find clear observational evidence for the influence of GES on the Far-side: it hosts the same metal-rich component peaked at [Fe/H] ~ -1.4, and its metal-rich population (-1.7 < [Fe/H] <= -1.3) shows GES-typical features consistent with the Near-side, namely a "sausage"-shaped velocity distribution and a velocity anisotropy as high as beta ~ 0.8-0.9. Action-space analysis shows that 10.86% +/- 0.23% of Far-side stars carry the GES dynamical imprint, consistent with 11.56% +/- 0.16% on the Near-side. The Far-side shows a residual prograde rotation that persists under increasingly aggressive disk-removal cuts, indicating a genuine kinematic signal rather than disk contamination, and a battery of robustness tests confirms that the symmetry is not an artifact of measurement uncertainties, residual disk contamination, or incomplete Sagittarius-stream removal. These results demonstrate that GES shaped the entire inner halo (r < 28 kpc) globally and symmetrically, with its imprint clearly present on the Far-side as well as the Near-side.
