papers.title: Cross-User Adaptation for sEMG Gesture Recognition via Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Prosthetic and assistive interfaces increasingly depend on decoding hand gestures from surface electromyography (sEMG). Because the signal is shaped by person-specific factors, the recurrent neural networks (RNNs) commonly used to model these temporal streams must adapt to new wearers and new gesture classes after deployment. Continual learning (CL) enables this adaptation without retraining from scratch, yet applying it to recurrent sEMG models is not straightforward. Standard recurrent training practices can destabilize learning, and which CL strategy holds up under realistic cross-user drift is unestablished. We evaluate three representative CL strategies under domain- and class-incremental drift on NinaPro DB1, and find experience replay to outperform elastic weight consolidation (EWC) and naive fine-tuning. It reaches 83.3% final accuracy for class-incremental drift while limiting forgetting to 1.8-5.8% accuracy drop, as against 16.2-28.5% for EWC and naive training. We further show these models must be trained on shuffled, independently-windowed segments. Streaming windows in temporal order collapses the network into predicting a single dominant gesture, while a shuffled, stateless regime trains stably. Finally, hand-crafted time-domain features raise per-task accuracy by up to about 40% over raw signals, but only replay preserves that gain under class-incremental drift.

papers.title: The Information Geometry of Representation Formation
papers.abstract: Most analyses of neural representations focus on trained endpoints, leaving the process by which internal structure forms comparatively unmeasured. We instead treat representation formation itself as an object of study, asking whether the path a representation takes through training reveals information that its endpoint does not. We formalize this idea by viewing representation learning as a geometric trajectory, using Bures geometry to measure movement through representation space and quantum Fisher information to characterize local sensitivity to input factors. We find that learning concentrates local sensitivity on task-relevant factors, and that changing only the prediction target reorganizes this geometry around the corresponding visual factor. More strikingly, representation trajectories become systematically less direct as the learned computation requires higher-order interactions among input factors. This effect persists under matched-performance and training-duration controls and transfers from synthetic vector inputs to residual CNNs on rendered and natural images. Importantly, formation history contains predictive information about the stability of the learned representation: controlling for interaction order, path tortuosity predicts its subsequent drift under continued training and sensitivity to parameter perturbations, whereas endpoint displacement does not. Finally, representation-aware optimization lets us actively shape these trajectories, showing that formation geometry is not only measurable but actionable. Together, these results establish representation formation as a new source of information about learning: its geometry reveals properties of the computation being constructed, predicts subsequent representational stability, and provides a target for intervention during optimization.

papers.title: Explaining Navigation Decisions: Stage-Aware Visual Attribution for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly enable robots to follow language instructions, understanding their navigation decisions becomes important for reliable deployment. Existing explainability methods overlook a key challenge in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN): evidence for the current action may be distributed across historical and current observations and associated with different instruction stages. We identify instruction-stage insensitivity, where existing methods produce similar explanations despite changes across different navigation stages. To address this issue, we propose a stage-aware attribution framework for VLN. We first construct action-conditioned temporal instruction--visual attributions across observations. These attributions are projected into instruction space to estimate stage associations, which guide the aggregation of relevant historical evidence for refining the current explanation. An instruction-guided spatial filter further suppresses isolated responses while preserving compact, instruction-relevant regions. Experiments across multiple VLN policies and benchmarks show improved attribution quality over existing methods. We further demonstrate that our method acts as a diagnostic tool for analyzing failure cases, and validate its applicability to real-world navigation on a Unitree G1 robot.

papers.title: Fovea-JEPA: Overcoming Geometric Blind Spots in V-JEPA for Camera Motion Recognition
papers.abstract: Camera motion recognition requires separating viewpoint changes caused by camera translation, rotation, or zoom from object motion and scene dynamics. Video-language models often rely on semantic cues and struggle with the geometric evidence needed for this task. Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures such as V-JEPA offer strong spatio-temporal representations, but our experiments suggest that they underrepresent geometric cues in some regions. Under temporal-reversal supervision, V-JEPA improves overall but degrades on several motion families, whereas a weaker geometry-oriented VGGT predictor improves across all families. We refer to these geometrically underrepresented regions as geometric blind spots and propose Fovea-JEPA to identify and address them. Using V-JEPA as the base model and VGGT as a geometry expert, we construct intervention pseudo-labels from their prediction errors to weakly supervise a blind-spot predictor. The predictor produces token-wise response maps, which are aggregated into a clip-level intervention score to guide adaptive fusion of visual and geometric features. This selective intervention introduces complementary geometric information while preserving reliable visual predictions. Experiments on CameraMotionDataset, CameraBench, and ShotBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Fovea-JEPA, with gains of 9.67, 8.67, and 24.38 percentage points over previously reported state-of-the-art baselines, respectively. Code and models will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Enabling Motion-Induced WiFi-CSI Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems: A Simulation Framework
papers.abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) enables fine-grained sensing of spatial relationships between wireless devices. The WiFi Sensor for Robotics (WSR) toolbox demonstrated that WiFi-CSI measurements collected during robot motion, combined with odometry, can be used to synthesize virtual antenna arrays, enabling motion-induced bearing estimation in multi-robot experiments. However, deploying the WSR approach has remained challenging due to its limited integration with standard robotics tools and reliance on deprecated WiFi-CSI acquisition hardware. This work presents an open-source simulation framework that integrates the WSR sensing pipeline within the robotic simulator Gazebo. The framework generates synthetic WiFi-CSI measurements with realistic physical signal properties and leverages realistic robot motion required for motion-induced sensing and downstream localization. It further supports processing both simulated and real WiFi-CSI data for direct comparison and validation. Our aim is to make WSR-style sensing accessible as a modular sensing modality for robotic research. We validate our framework by comparing simulated and real-world experiments using TurtleBot3 robots, and demonstrate its use for bearing estimation and robot localization. This work lowers the barrier to entry for WiFi-CSI-based sensing in multi-robot systems and provides a foundation for integrating WiFi-CSI sensing with multi-modal perception for localization and coordination. All code and experimental details are publicly available at https://github.com/baharhaghighat/DARS_2026_Dijkstra_et_al

papers.title: What Sketches Tell Us about LVLMs: Conventions, Grounding, and Localisation
papers.abstract: LVLM benchmarks tell us whether a model answers correctly, but not which visual conventions it has retained, nor where those conventions live. Sketches expose this hidden structure. A sketch removes texture, lighting, and photographic context while preserving the strokes humans judged sufficient for recognition. If an LVLM can operate on that abstraction, the surviving signal is structural rather than merely photometric. We introduce a training-free sketch probe with three readouts: temporal part-construction order, spatial attention-based grounding, and the mechanistic layer/head locus of grounding. We evaluate nine LVLMs on part order and five on the attention readouts, over two part-annotated sketch datasets. Three findings emerge. First, LVLM part order tracks human convention: models reproduce canonical orderings where human drawings converge, and become correspondingly variable where human orderings vary. Controls that blank, withhold, and mismatch the sketch locate this convention in the language model. Second, part-level grounding survives the abstraction: attention heads selected from the frozen model with an existing recipe recover part and object regions on object and scene sketches, with no grounding supervision. Third, the grounding signal concentrates in a narrow mid-network band whose location follows the base language model rather than parameter count in the two families we compare, and remains stable across object and scene sketches. The result is a practical diagnostic for sketch-driven LVLMs: no fine-tuning, no auxiliary segmenter, and a layer band that doubles as a head-selection prior, matching or improving grounding mAcc@0.1 in every model and dataset we tested.

papers.title: Cut a Wall, See a Wall: Identity Substitution in Occluded Point-Cloud Perception for Construction Robots
papers.abstract: Construction robots must label building elements they can only partly see. We show that when occlusion at test time removes whole regions of a scene, rather than parts of an object as in training, point-cloud segmentation networks do not simply miss the hidden elements: they relabel them, and the errors collapse onto a single sink class. With fixed synthetic layouts the column absorbs up to 70% of all test points; with randomized layouts the sink moves to the stair, predicted at 4.5-5.4x its true share across three training seeds. Baseline mIoU falls to 0.15-0.27 (fixed) and 0.36-0.72 (randomized), and up to 269 whole objects vanish in a single test set. Appending 14 hand-computed geometric features per point (GPE) restores mIoU to 0.54-0.92 and removes 64-100% of whole-object losses in every run, for PointNet++ and a PTv3-style transformer in both layout regimes; on real S3DIS scans it removes every whole-wall loss (10 to 0). In an as-built column check computed from the predictions, GPE raises the share of correctly checked views from 17-58% to 71-92%. Feature permutation on fixed, randomized and real scenes explains the pattern: each class relies on whichever cue is stable in its training data, position for height-banded slabs and beams, intrinsic shape for walls and stairs once their position varies. Occlusion augmentation is a strong alternative on mIoU, but in every setting it loses more whole objects than GPE (e.g., 25-35 vs. 0).

papers.title: T-ConSG: A LiDAR-Based Real-Time Temporal Construction Scene Graph for Dynamic and Evolving Environments
papers.abstract: Dynamic and continuously evolving environments present significant challenges for robotic mapping and scene understanding, particularly on construction sites where moving agents, temporary obstacles, and persistent structural changes coexist. While dynamic and long-term SLAM methods can detect motion and environmental changes, their outputs are predominantly metric representations that provide limited structure for higher-level spatial and temporal reasoning. This paper presents a LiDAR-based real-time temporal construction scene graph (T-ConSG) that jointly represents free-space regions, static objects, dynamic objects, and environmental events with spatial-relational and event-participation edges. The proposed framework incrementally constructs the graph from LiDAR-derived geometric evidence, maintaining persistent free-space and static-object information while tracking dynamic objects. Changes in accumulated spatial evidence are further represented as explicit installation and removal events, allowing the graph to capture both transient dynamics and persistent environmental evolution. We demonstrate the proposed representation through three complementary application studies: dynamics-aware navigation in a bricklaying testbed, construction progress monitoring on the ConSLAM dataset, and online change detection in a simulated construction environment. The results demonstrate that the proposed T-ConSG provides a unified representation for organizing spatial and temporal information and supports robotic reasoning across environments containing both short-term dynamics and persistent changes.

history_evidence.official_title: T-ConSG: A LiDAR-Based Real-Time Temporal Construction Scene Graph for Dynamic and Evolving Environments
history_evidence.official_abstract: Dynamic and continuously evolving environments present significant challenges for robotic mapping and scene understanding, particularly on construction sites where moving agents, temporary obstacles, and persistent structural changes coexist. While dynamic and long-term SLAM methods can detect motion and environmental changes, their outputs are predominantly metric representations that provide limited structure for higher-level spatial and temporal reasoning. This paper presents a LiDAR-based real-time temporal construction scene graph (T-ConSG) that jointly represents free-space regions, static objects, dynamic objects, and environmental events with spatial-relational and event-participation edges. The proposed framework incrementally constructs the graph from LiDAR-derived geometric evidence, maintaining persistent free-space and static-object information while tracking dynamic objects. Changes in accumulated spatial evidence are further represented as explicit installation and removal events, allowing the graph to capture both transient dynamics and persistent environmental evolution. We demonstrate the proposed representation through three complementary application studies: dynamics-aware navigation in a bricklaying testbed, construction progress monitoring on the ConSLAM dataset, and online change detection in a simulated construction environment. The results demonstrate that the proposed T-ConSG provides a unified representation for organizing spatial and temporal information and supports robotic reasoning across environments containing both short-term dynamics and persistent changes.

papers.title: Extended LASMP: Language Aided Subset Sampling Based Motion Planner for Drone Navigation
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a command-aligned sampling distribution that incorporates navigation commands directly into the exploration process to improve the efficiency of sampling-based motion planning for quadcopters in three-dimensional environments. Inspired by the Language-Aided Subset Sampling Motion Planner, this paper extends command-aware subset sampling to aerial systems. Subset sampling is generalized to command-aligned regions, enabling structured 3D exploration while preserving probabilistic completeness. Natural language instructions are grounded into yaw-conditioned and altitude-aware geometric constraints using a prompt-based large language model for entity extraction and instruction validation. Extensive simulations in complex environments demonstrate that the proposed method generates collision-free, consistent trajectories while significantly reducing sampling effort compared to uniform RRT-based planners.

papers.title: Lightweight Change Detection for Adaptive Collective Perception in Dynamic Environments
papers.abstract: Swarm robotics enables scalable inspection through collective perception, where robots infer environmental properties from distributed observations. A common benchmark considers robots exploring black-white tiled environments and determining the majority tile type. While most work studies static environments, dynamic environments remain underexplored. We study collective perception in dynamic environments where the tile proportion and the spatial correlation of surface patterns may change over time. To enable implementation on resource-constrained robots, we integrate a lightweight change detection mechanism into a Bayesian collective decision-making framework that resets robot beliefs when distribution shifts are detected. The proposed detector requires constant memory and constant per-sample computation, unlike two recent competitive approaches that store the full sample stream, making it suitable for memory-constrained robots. We further introduce a method that detects spatially correlated sampling and adapts sampling intervals online to mitigate correlation effects. Our simulation results in Webots show competitive change detection delays, more consistent precision across communication settings, and improved decision accuracy under changing spatial correlations.

papers.title: Learning Interaction-Aware Path Corrections from Unlabeled Trajectories: A LiDAR-Based Sim-to-Real GNN Framework for Construction Robots
papers.abstract: Construction robots operating near workers require navigation that can anticipate human motion while remaining robust to dynamic and unstructured site conditions. However, existing social navigation methods depend on hand-crafted interaction rules, labeled demonstrations, or robot-specific control policies, limiting their scalability and transferability in construction environments. We propose a real-time, LiDAR-only framework that learns interaction-aware path corrections from unlabeled demonstrations. Constant-velocity extrapolation generates residual learning targets, while a GNN models relationships among the robot, pedestrians, and goal context. During deployment, an extended Kalman filter tracks LiDAR detections to construct dynamic graphs, and the GNN offsets planner-generated waypoints through a planner-agnostic interface. Within the bricklaying trial, the GNN reduced path irregularity by 39.2\% and increased minimum TTC. Across Dynablox sequences, it increased minimum TTC by 38.3\% while producing shorter, smoother paths than the baselines. Ablation studies supported a 1.0-s prediction interval and confirmed the benefits of target context, reflection augmentation, and feature normalization.

papers.title: Stochastic quantization and Osterwalder-Schrader axioms for quantum field theory models
papers.abstract: This PhD thesis constructs the $P(Φ)_2$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathscr{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We first construct the finite-volume measure of the $P(Φ)_2$ model on $\mathscr{D}'(\mathbb{S}_R)$, where $\mathbb{S}_R$ is a two-dimensional sphere of radius $R\in\mathbb{N}_+$. To this end, we rely on Nelson's hypercontractivity estimate. We then use parabolic stochastic quantization and the energy method to construct the infinite-volume measure on $\mathscr{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$. This requires establishing the global-in-time existence of solutions to the corresponding stochastic partial differential equations with fixed cutoffs. The remainder of the thesis is devoted to verifying the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms: regularity, reflection positivity, and invariance under translations, rotations, and reflections. This combination of axioms, which is crucial for obtaining a non-trivial local relativistic quantum field theory on Minkowski spacetime, had not been established in earlier constructions based on stochastic quantization.

papers.title: Spectral Turán problems for complete bipartite expansions in linear hypergraphs
papers.abstract: An $r$-uniform hypergraph is linear if any two edges share at most one vertex. For a family $\mathcal F$ of $r$-graphs, let $\text{ex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,\mathcal F)$ denote, respectively, the maximum number of edges and the maximum spectral radius of an $n$-vertex $\mathcal F$-free linear $r$-graph. In this paper, we show that for $t\ge s\ge3$, $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})\le \frac{(t-s+1)^{1/s}}{r-1}n^{1-1/s}+o(n^{1-1/s})$, where $K_{s,t}^{+}$ is the $r$-graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{s,t}$ by enlarging each edge with $r-2$ new vertices. This answers a problem of She, Fan and Kang in a stronger form. Moreover, our result implies that $\text{ex}^\text{lin}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+}) \le \frac{(t-s+1)^{1/s}}{r(r-1)}n^{2-1/s}+o(n^{2-1/s})$, which improves the leading coefficient in the corresponding bound of Gao and Chang. We also give a construction which implies that $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})=Θ(n^{1-1/s})$ and $\text{ex}^\text{lin}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})=Θ(n^{2-1/s})$ for $s\ge 4r-6$ and $t>(s-1)!$.

papers.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. Through a large-scale evaluation across multiple benchmarks and model backbones, we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value. Taking RAG as a reference, we dissect the net value of memory into the gains and losses over direct retrieval, termed memory benefit and memory tax. These gains and losses arise because memory process changes how the raw information is organized and accessed. We view such changes as the double-edged deviations from the raw history. They are originally designed and introduced to benefit the task, for example by reorganizing facts or distilling preferences, but some may also remove or obscure evidence, giving rise to memory tax. Since memory benefit reflects the expected gains of its design, we then focus more on the overlooked memory tax, study how it arises from the system and evaluation side, and generalize the concept to more application scenarios of memory. We hope the notion of memory tax can provide a new lens and shift more attention from standalone performance to the net value of memory, informing more reliable memory designs and evaluations. We will open-source the code and results to the community. Project Page: https://hexuan21.github.io/MemoryTax/

papers.title: Bi-Objective Receding-Horizon Scheduling of Nurses and Hospital Service Robots
papers.abstract: This paper studies the joint scheduling of nurses and hospital service robots as a bi-objective mixed-integer linear programming problem. The formulation represents heterogeneous nursing skills, alternative skill-coverage modes, nurse availability and temporal rules, workload balance, robot task capability, charging and battery dynamics, and human supervision. Robot workload relief is credited only when an eligible service is actually executed, and explicit supervision-load variables deduct the corresponding nurse capacity from clinical coverage. The receding-horizon formulation also includes a cross-window night--morning constraint and a terminal battery reserve. The computational study is presented as numerical verification on synthetic hospital-like instances rather than clinical validation. Under the proposed formulation, the eight-nurse reference case gives $Z_1=0.78$ and $Z_2=3.164$. A common-budget comparison on B20 seed~1 yields total shortage $53.70$ for the integrated model, compared with $58.03$ for sequential nurse--robot scheduling and $59.46$ for the nurse-only baseline. Additional experiments examine multiple epsilon budgets on a larger B30 instance, sensitivity to robot-relief/supervision parameters and objective weights, and one-day versus two-day rolling horizons against a static full-horizon reference. The battery and routing representations remain aggregate planning approximations, and the scalability evidence is interpreted accordingly. No patient records or real hospital staff data are used, so the results establish model behavior and comparative numerical evidence rather than practical clinical effectiveness.

papers.title: Planetesimal Delivery to Giant Planet Circumplanetary Disks: Bulk Ice Enrichment and an Ice-rich Iapetus
papers.abstract: The regular satellites of Jupiter and Saturn are substantially enriched in ice relative to the rock-rich solids of the outer Solar System. In addition, the satellites interior to Titan and distant Iapetus are icier than Titan itself. Collisional processes and subsequent migration can readily alter compositions deep in the planetary potential well, but producing a distant, ice-rich satellite with Iapetus's radius of about 700 km is a challenge \citep{mosqueira2026a}. We show that differential ablation and capture of icy and rocky fragments from differentiated outer Solar System bodies can explain the bulk Jovian and Kronian satellite ice enrichment and supply the substantial ice-rich inventory needed for Iapetus. For 1\,m--1\,km fragments with the canonical size-distribution index \(p=3.5\) and a source containing 30\% ice by mass, the fixed radial distance Saturn calculation deposits material with ice fractions of 0.66 (delivery of vapor-only rock) or 0.50 (with retained rock melt) at 20 Saturn radii and nearly pure ice at 60 Saturn radii. Following three-dimensional trajectories over repeated passages through the pressure-supported gas gives ice fractions of about 0.4 near 20 Saturn radii and 0.9 near 60 Saturn radii. The matching Jupiter calculation yields a similar bulk ice enrichment, with a corresponding compositional gradient across the Galilean satellite region. These delivery profiles supply ice-enriched material for satellite formation. Yet satellitesimal inward migration subsequently modifies the material incorporated into satellites and thus alters their bulk compositions. We briefly discuss the implications for the PDS~70 planetary system.

papers.title: DSGN: A Dual-Stream Gated Network for Scalable Simultaneous Surveillance and Containment
papers.abstract: The simultaneous surveillance and containment (SSC) problem arises in multi-robot applications such as perimeter security and environmental monitoring, where robots must survey a region of interest and coordinate to enclose targets once they are detected. Surveillance favors spatial dispersion for coverage, whereas containment requires target-centric cohesion for enclosure. This conflict makes heuristic switching unstable, and the instability becomes more pronounced as larger robotic networks introduce more inter-agent and agent-target relations. End-to-end DRL reduces reliance on hand-crafted switching, but conventional single-stream policies often mix surveillance and containment cues in one shared feature space that could entangle dispersion-oriented and target-centric signals and weaken task transitions. In this paper, we propose the Dual-Stream Gated Network (DSGN), an architecture designed to address scale-amplified task-transition difficulties by separating surveillance and containment into specialized representation streams and coordinating them through a context-aware gating mechanism. A probabilistic prior further regularizes the gating process, reducing ambiguous intermediate decisions and supporting clearer behavioral transitions under large-scale interaction complexity. Evaluations show that DSGN maintains strong task efficacy and scalability under constant-density cross-scale settings. Additional ablation and phase-specific evaluations show that the proposed dynamic gating mechanism and probabilistic prior support effective task arbitration and reliable mode switching in both pure surveillance and task-switching scenarios. The source code is available at https://github.com/zuozysama/DSGN.

papers.title: Doppler-aided Position-Velocity Tracking of Hidden Objects using mmWave Radar
papers.abstract: Safe indoor operation requires autonomous tracking of objects that are not directly visible to the robot. Optical non-line-of-sight (NLoS) methods depend on ambient lighting and scene geometry or on weak multi-bounce returns that need long acquisitions. Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar offers an attractive alternative: walls act as reflectors for mmWave signals, and frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radars enable fast, practical measurement of range, angle, and velocity. However, the low resolution of these radars leads to spatially ambiguous observations. papers.title: Secure Integrated Sensing and Communications with Movable Beyond-Diagonal RIS
papers.abstract: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), when the sensed target is itself an eavesdropper, the illumination required for sensing coincides with the leakage that secrecy must suppress. This paper shows how a beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) with movable elements decouples the two tasks in a monostatic setting, where the echo returns to the base station through the surface. We prove that a lossless reciprocal BD-RIS maps $K$ incident fields onto $K$ prescribed fields if and only if the two sets share the same Gram matrix and their bilinear Gram matrix is symmetric; unlike a diagonal RIS, it can thus steer a two-dimensional incident subspace onto any prescribed subspace. With a single stream, sensing incurs an unavoidable rate loss, whereas a closed-form zero-forcing design with a confidential and a Gaussian sensing stream nulls the data at the target and the sensing at the user, so that sensing costs only an SNR offset. Since all variables follow in closed form for any placement, the joint design reduces to a monotone search over the element positions, without alternating optimization. Simulations show that the dual-stream design loses only $1.1$ bit/s/Hz when the sensing requirement grows by $30$ dB, against $8.3$ bit/s/Hz for a single stream, while movement, interconnection, and the robust derivative-null design add up to $1.9$, $0.9$, and $2.6$ bit/s/Hz, respectively.

papers.title: LegoOcc++: Towards Consistent Open-Vocabulary 3D Occupancy Prediction
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction is important for embodied agents operating in complex environments whose semantic categories extend beyond fixed taxonomies. While recent studies have explored open-vocabulary occupancy in outdoor driving scenarios, indoor environments remain challenging due to dense occlusions, complex geometry, and fine-grained long-tailed semantics. To reduce the need for expensive voxel-level semantic annotations, we study a geometry-only supervision setting requiring only binary occupancy labels. We build upon Language-Embedded Gaussians as a unified representation coupling 3D geometry with language-aligned semantics. For geometry learning, we introduce an opacity-aware Poisson-based Gaussian-to-Occupancy formulation that enables stable volumetric aggregation under binary occupancy supervision. For semantic learning, we render Gaussian features into images and align them with a frozen open-vocabulary model, together with Progressive Temperature Decay to reduce feature mixing during Gaussian splatting. Building on this framework, we further introduce Instance-Level Semantic Consistency to alleviate fragmented object predictions, and Covisibility-Aware Support-View Selection to provide informative and less redundant multi-view semantic supervision. We also extend our framework to outdoor driving scenarios to evaluate its generality across substantially different environments. Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves strong open-vocabulary occupancy performance, validating the effectiveness and generality of our framework. Code will be available at https://github.com/JuIvyy/LegoOcc.

papers.title: A Nearly Optimal Min-Cut Algorithm for Dynamic Streams
papers.abstract: We give an $\tilde{O}(n/\varepsilon)$-space algorithm for the minimum cut problem in dynamic streams, resolving the space complexity of streaming min-cut up to polylogarithmic factors. Ding, Garces, Li, Lin, Nelson, Shah, and Woodruff (ITCS 2025) obtained the same $\tilde{O}(n/\varepsilon)$ space bound for insertion-only streams, while prior to our work the best known bound even for unweighted dynamic streams was $\tilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^2)$, due to Ahn, Guha, and McGregor (PODS 2012). Our main technical contribution is an $\tilde{O}(n/\varepsilon)$-space for-each cut sketch in dynamic streams, which may be of independent interest. The construction applies to weighted graphs under general $\pmΔ$ updates, a stronger model than the standard dynamic-stream setting in which weighted edges are inserted and deleted in their entirety. Despite this stronger guarantee, our algorithm is surprisingly simple and relies on very little machinery. We also obtain applications to minimum $\ell_p$-norm $k$-partitioning for every fixed $k$, weighted correlation-clustering evaluation for two clusters, and for-each cut sketching in balanced directed graphs.

papers.title: Post-fragmentation Morphological and Broadband Color Evolution of C/2025 K1 (ATLAS)
papers.abstract: Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) underwent major fragmentation after its 2025 October 8 perihelion passage at q ~ 0.33 au. We evaluated 324 profile-extraction configurations and removed solutions whose localized peak landed on the search-window boundary. The fragment-axis surface-brightness enhancement relocates inward between November 26 and 29 and outward between December 5 and 8; the sign of both changes is recovered in every valid configuration and at all tested common target PSFs from 5.3 to 6.0 arcsec. Calibrated BVR photometry using Gaia DR3 synthetic Johnson-Kron-Cousins standards independently shows a repeatable November 26-29 change in broadband spectral shape: B-V decreases while V-R increases. The curvature index S'_(V-R) - S'_(B-V) changes by +3.47 (+1.50/-1.65) percent per 1000 Angstrom, with 99.1 percent of Monte Carlo realizations positive, while the full B-R reflectivity gradient remains approximately constant. Repeating the color comparison at a fixed projected radius of 2205 km produces nearly identical changes. The combined results are consistent with continued restructuring of the unresolved post-fragmentation inner coma, while broadband imaging alone cannot uniquely separate dust-color evolution, molecular emission, and changing contributions from unresolved fragments.

papers.title: RoboDuo: Attempt, Check and Atomic Recovery through Code for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map a language instruction and the current observation directly to actions, without checking whether the instruction has been completed. For long-horizon tasks, a single failed step therefore goes unnoticed and leaves the whole task unfinished. Such failed episodes, however, often end with the task partially complete. Moreover, the unfinished steps are reusable atomic skills that recur across demonstrations. A failed attempt can thus be recovered by composing with atomic skills. We propose RoboDuo, a closed-loop dual-system framework that uses code as the interface between a coding agent and two VLAs. The agent writes a program that lets a full-task VLA attempt the whole task and checks whether it is complete; on failure, an atomic VLA finishes the remaining steps. Since the agent emits no actions and only decides which VLA for execution, RoboDuo wraps an existing full-task VLA without updating its weights. To train the atomic VLA and the coding agent with the completion-checking ability, we build LIBERO-Atomic, LIBERO-Code, and LIBERO-Judge from a single set of LIBERO demonstrations. RoboDuo consistently improves X-VLA and $π_{0.5}$ on LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO, with the largest gains on long-horizon tasks, and recovers failed rollouts of a frozen full-task VLA on a real robot.

papers.title: Geo-Filtered Approximate Nearest-Neighbor Search on a Single Proximity Graph
papers.abstract: Geo-filtered approximate nearest-neighbor (GFANN) search retrieves the objects inside a query-specified geographic disk whose feature vectors are closest to a query vector, a core operation in location-aware Web search. A disk filter on a standard proximity graph invalidates out-of-disk routing vertices; on selective disks, these removals break greedy paths and recall drops sharply. Existing methods scan all in-disk objects, over-fetch unfiltered candidates, or maintain separate sub-indexes across spatial partitions, trading latency for index overhead. We propose REACH, a single-graph index based on row-local active-order invariance: if every vertex stores its outgoing neighbors in a fixed-width row sorted by vector distance, any disk filter masks out-of-disk entries while surviving in-disk (active) neighbors remain vector-sorted. Offline, each vertex merges globally closest vector candidates with a nearest-first geographic stream into one row; online, beam search evaluates vector distances only for the first l active entries of each visited row. Because co-located objects share the same distance to every query center, every disk admits a coordinate group in full or not at all, decomposing active connectivity into intra-group and inter-coordinate conditions. Under a spatial marked-site model with repeated coordinates, we prove that polylogarithmic out-degree guarantees strong connectivity across all disks and constant-factor distance reduction per hop on compact disks, while a cut-rank threshold characterizes the minimum scan budget l. Across four datasets up to 10^7 objects, one REACH index per dataset outperforms SOTA methods, achieving 2.49x higher geometric-mean QPS than the strongest baseline at 0.95 Recall@10 on selective queries, while building 3.8x-11.9x faster and using 37%-45% less space than a SOTA spatial-graph index.

papers.title: Functional Superoscillations in a Wave Processor
papers.abstract: Physical wave processors are constrained by diffraction, but the bandwidth of the mathematical functions they implement need not be set by it. Here, we demonstrate continuous and multiplexed optical processing of superoscillatory functions, in which a scalar argument is encoded onto a wavefront and a fixed diffractive wave processor synthesizes optical responses that approximate the corresponding function outputs in parallel. Unlike conventional superoscillatory optics that generates predetermined fields, superoscillation here is expressed in the input-output dependence on the encoded argument. Its frequencies are therefore distinct from the transverse spatial frequencies of propagating light and are not subject to the same diffraction-imposed cutoff. We demonstrate complex-valued superoscillatory function synthesis and introduce a multiplexed architecture that simultaneously evaluates distinct target superoscillatory functions whose harmonic content exceeds that of the optical input encoding. Visible-light experiments further validate this beyond-encoding superoscillatory regime. Together, these results establish functional superoscillation as a design principle for wave-based computation and show how interference, diffractive depth and spatial channel allocation extend the functional reach of passive wave processors. More broadly, these analyses establish a separation between functional bandwidth and physical wave bandwidth in analog optical computation.

papers.title: StickFigure: Enabling Pose-Only IoT Cameras for Privacy-Preserving Edge Vision
papers.abstract: Indoor IoT cameras can support assisted living and activity-aware spaces, but exporting raw RGB frames raises privacy concerns by exposing facial, clothing, and household details that body-motion tasks often do not require. To overcome these challenges and enable on-device pose streams on (almost) any IoT camera, we present two core designs in StickFigure: an activation-aware pose backbone that allocates channel capacity after spatial downsampling and a lightweight hierarchical MLP refiner that selectively corrects elbow and wrist coordinates using intermediate visual features and kinematic context. We fully implement StickFigure and evaluate it on public benchmarks and real-world deployment. Compared with state-of-the-art MCU pose models, StickFigure achieves the highest pose accuracy and downstream HAR utility on both NTU RGB+D and Penn Action, while using 96.5% fewer parameters and 99.3% fewer MACs per frame than RTMPose-S-based baselines, achieving 0.107 s p95 latency on a representative STM32H753 MCU. We believe StickFigure establishes a new operating point for privacy-aware edge vision on massive IoT cameras.

papers.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions of the compressible MHD equations on the half space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the global well-posedness and large-time asymptotic behavior of strong solutions to the $n$-dimensional ($n\ge 2$) compressible viscous resistive magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}_+^n$. We impose the standard no-slip boundary condition on the velocity field and two types of physically relevant boundary conditions on the magnetic field: the insulating boundary condition and the perfectly conducting boundary condition. Under the assumption that the initial data are small perturbations of the constant equilibrium state $(\barρ, \mathbf{0}, \mathbf{0})$, we first establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions in Sobolev spaces by deriving uniform energy estimates and using a bootstrapping argument. Then, by combining the sharp decay estimates of solutions to the corresponding linearized system with Duhamel's principle, we obtain the decay rates of solutions to the nonlinear problem. Specifically, we prove that the solutions decay at the rate $t^{-\frac{n}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{p}\right)}$ in $L^p$ norm for $2\le p\le\infty$, and we also establish the decay rates of their first-order derivatives. Furthermore, we show that the global solutions converge to the linearized solutions with an improved decay rate as time goes to infinity. Our results extend the classical results of Kagei and Kobayashi \cite{Kagei-Kobayashi2002, Kagei-Kobayashi2005} for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the half space to the compressible MHD system with both insulating and perfectly conducting boundary conditions.

papers.abstract: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $θ$ and $η$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $θ$ and $η$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.

papers.title: Write What Matters: Disentangling Token Selection from Slot Allocation in Recurrent Memory
papers.abstract: Long-sequence models must retain earlier information. Full attention keeps all past tokens but grows expensive, and recurrent-memory models compress history into fixed slots for linear-time processing. Limited capacity makes writes consequential: distractors can interfere with useful content, while skipped evidence cannot be recalled. Existing multi-slot memories write every token to the same number of slots, merging whether to store it with how many slots to update. We introduce Factorized Write Routing (FWR), which first keeps or skips each token and then chooses a fixed or token-adaptive number of slots. Queries still read all slots. Across ten seeds on two synthetic tasks that query facts after long contexts, we observe a density-dependent reversal. With four slots per write, long-context accuracy favors always writing on dense Feature Recall (0.472 vs 0.337), but learned selective writing on sparse-fact Passkey (0.222 vs 0.048). The tested adaptive rule underperforms fixed allocation under the learned gate on both tasks. A diagnostic oracle given fact labels unavailable at deployment reaches 0.372 on Passkey, showing headroom in filtering distractors. The results suggest avoiding missed writes in information-dense contexts and filtering distractors when they dominate.

papers.title: AudioFM: Towards General Purpose Audio Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Learning audio representations that effectively bridge holistic global soundscapes with fine-grained acoustic moments is a long-standing goal in self-supervised learning. Recording-level contrastive objectives encourage agreement between pooled audio representations, but do not explicitly supervise local time-frequency representations. We introduce AudioFM, a self-supervised framework that combines recording-level contrast with patch-wise masked latent discrimination. Using visible acoustic context, a student predicts representations of masked patches and identifies their corresponding full-view teacher targets among candidates from other recordings. We further incorporate weaker supervision from eligible temporal neighbors to encourage local temporal consistency. Extensive evaluations show that AudioFM achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse audio domains in linear probing, fine-tuning, and zero-shot transfer, demonstrating superior event detection, robust scene-level understanding, and strong domain generalizability.

papers.title: Evaluating Wi-Fi HaLow for Next-Generation Capsule Endoscopy
papers.abstract: Capsule endoscopy is limited by its wireless link: insufficient throughput restricts image resolution and frame rate, whereas high-rate radios typically use higher carrier frequencies that experience greater attenuation through tissue. This work evaluates Wi-Fi HaLow (IEEE 802.11ah), a sub-GHz Wi-Fi standard, as an image link for capsule endoscopy. Across all tested combinations of modulation and coding scheme and bandwidth, the saturation TCP throughput reached 15.55 Mbps, and the fastest configuration also achieved the lowest energy per bit. Through power optimization strategies, the combined power consumption of the HaLow module and microcontroller at 1 frame per second (FPS) was reduced from 101.70 to 14.00 mW, which is comparable to that of Bluetooth Low Energy systems. In a simulated in vivo setting, the default rate control selected the highest tested MCS and bandwidth, indicating sufficient link quality; this configuration also had the lowest measured power in both the 1 FPS mode (13.59 mW) and the 30 FPS mode (174.21 mW). The capsule-to-receiver latency was 20.68 ms for a 24 KB frame, while the receiver-to-capsule latency was 4.77 ms for a command; this low-latency bidirectional communication supports real-time detection and manipulation for next-generation capsule endoscopy.

papers.title: GeoPrompt: Geometry-Conditioned Prompt Learning for Underwater Open-Vocabulary Instance Segmentation
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary instance segmentation (OVIS) provides a promising solution for marine perception by recognizing and segmenting categories beyond predefined label spaces. Existing OVIS methods usually rely on vision-language alignment, where visual region features are matched with textual category embeddings to recognize both seen and unseen classes. However, this alignment assumption becomes fragile in underwater environments. Color attenuation, scattering, turbidity, and low contrast distort visual appearance, causing region features to deviate from their corresponding semantic concepts. As a result, the similarity between degraded visual features and textual classifiers becomes unreliable, which particularly weakens the recognition of unseen underwater categories that cannot be corrected by category-specific supervision. To address these issues, we propose GeoPrompt, a geometry-conditioned prompt learning framework for underwater open-vocabulary instance segmentation. Our key insight is that geometric structure is more stable than visual appearance in degraded underwater scenes. Specifically, GeoPrompt introduces a geometry-guided visual adaptation module (GVAM) to extract depth-derived structural priors and inject them into multi-scale visual features. It further develops a geometry-conditioned prompt learning (GCPL) that generates geometry-aware textual classifiers from structural representations. These geometry-aware classifiers are integrated with fixed and image-conditioned textual classifiers to improve open-vocabulary semantic alignment. Experiments on the MARIS-OpenIS benchmark show that GeoPrompt achieves state-of-the-art performance and brings consistent improvements on underwater open-vocabulary instance segmentation.

papers.title: Orbital stability of positive standing waves to the logarithmic Choquard equations
papers.abstract: The paper concerns the orbital stability of positive standing waves for the logarithmic Choquard equation with a small local nonlinear perturbation. First, the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of the positive ground-state solution are established via bifurcation and compactness arguments. Then, by exploiting the spectral properties of the linearized operator around the positive ground-state solution in high-energy spaces, the orbital stability of the corresponding positive standing wave is proved. The main difficulty in establishing orbital stability stems from the fact that the logarithmic convolution kernel is both sign-changing and strongly singular, while the norm used to prove global existence is not translation invariant. Consequently, existing approaches to orbital stability for positive ground-state solutions of three-and higher-dimensional Choquard equations with Riesz-type kernels cannot be applied to the two-dimensional logarithmic Choquard equation considered here.

papers.title: kstress: a LAMMPS package for calculating the 2D wavevector-dependent stress tensor and its anisotropy in amorphous solids
papers.abstract: The stress tensor resolved in wavevector $\qvec$ and time $t$, $σ_{αβ}(\qvec,t)$, gives access to the elastic moduli of amorphous solids as a function of the probed length scale, and to the long-range stress correlations that distinguish an amorphous solid from a liquid. Its evaluation requires the contribution of every interacting pair and therefore an interface to the force loop of the molecular dynamics code. In the current work, we present: i) an optimized implementation of the LAMMPS~\cite{lammps} module for calculating $σ_{αβ}(\qvec,t)$, in which trigonometric functions are calculated only for the basic wavevectors and, in addition, all the relevant wavevectors are supplied as an explicit list rather than generated as a full grid, so that only the wavevectors of interest are computed and stored, and ii) a validation protocol for the code illustrated for a two-dimensional polydisperse Lennard-Jones (2DpLJ) glass-forming liquid. Based on these technical achievements we elucidated how the affine moduli for the 2DpLJ model depend on the norm $q$ of the wavevector. In particular, we demonstrate that the longitudinal affine modulus shows a minimum near $q_\text{max}$ corresponding to the main peak of the structure factor. Our data also point to the peaks in the $q$-dependencies of vibrational frequencies well below $q_\text{max}$ for both transverse and longitudinal modes. The potential relevance of this feature to the ``boson peak'' is discussed as well.

papers.title: Sharp gradient comparison and rigidity for semilinear equations on manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove sharp amplitude and gradient comparisons for positive solutions of a class of semilinear elliptic equations on complete manifolds under a Ricci lower bound. Equality at one point characterizes hyperbolic space and the corresponding radial solution. The local estimates are uniform in the mixing coefficients and number of terms for positive mixtures of subcritical powers. For a class of conformal compactifications defined by a source equation, we obtain sharp boundary scalar-curvature bounds and hyperbolic rigidity. We also construct non-Einstein examples whose normalization persists under small compactly supported metric perturbations.

papers.title: From Presence Labels to Bounding Boxes: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Scale Surgical Instrument Localization?
papers.abstract: Spatial localization of surgical instruments through bounding-box annotations is a foundational component of surgical scene understanding, supporting detection, tracking, interaction analysis, and grounded vision-language applications. Yet existing annotations often cover selected frames, video subsets, or dataset variants rather than complete procedures. Manual extension is time-consuming and expert-dependent. Additionally, weakly supervised and detector-based pseudo-labels require task-specific training and may be imprecise. In this study, we design a scalable MLLM-based annotation framework that converts surgical frames and existing instrument-presence labels into accurate bounding boxes, and systematically analyze its reliability, cost, and design sensitivity. We instantiate the framework using six MLLMs and a multi-call configuration on laparoscopic cholecystectomy in Cholec80. Using a carefully designed stratification scheme, two annotators independently label 1,000 frames, and an expert surgeon reviews one annotation set to establish the reference. Results show that instrument-set F1 ranges from 88.2 to 92.7,whereas mIoU ranges from 0.180 to 0.735, showing that comparable recognition can conceal large localization differences. A structured multi-stage annotation pipeline achieves 0.784 mIoU, compared with 0.735 for the best single-call baseline and 0.814 human-human agreement. Using the best accuracy pipeline, we create and publicly release a spatial extension of Cholec80 comprising 285,977 bounding boxes across all 184,498 annotated frames from the 80 videos. The annotations and human references are made available on GitHub

papers.title: Single Camera based Simulation and Try-on Ready Avatar Modeling
papers.abstract: Reconstructing and rendering high-fidelity, animatable, and try-on-ready virtual avatars using only a single camera is crucial for many applications. However, existing try-on-ready human avatar reconstruction methods struggle to achieve this from monocular videos or single images, primarily due to two issues: (1) existing approaches typically use a single layer to represent both garments and the underlying body, ignoring their distinct motion characteristics; and (2) input captured from a single camera often fails to fully cover both the garments and the underlying body. To address these challenges, we propose a physically integrated, double-layer GS-Mesh representation for reconstructing decoupled 3D clothed human avatars from monocular videos or even single images by incorporating 2D generated data. While 2D generation methods can produce video sequences from given pose sequences, they struggle to maintain inter-frame consistency. We decompose the inter-frame inconsistencies in the generated data into geometric and appearance inconsistencies. Based on our 3D representation, we ensure that the final reconstruction and rendering results are both 3D-consistent and temporally coherent. Compared with existing 3D garment transfer methods that rely on multi-view reconstruction and most 2D approaches that use diffusion models for image-based garment editing without novel-view or novel-pose synthesis, our method requires only a monocular video or even a single image while producing visually plausible cloth dynamics during virtual try-on and novel-pose animation. This represents a significant advancement toward virtual try-on with visually plausible cloth dynamics using only a single camera.

papers.title: Quasicircularity of the Zakeri Curve and Capture Component Boundaries
papers.abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number of bounded type, we prove that the locus of critically marked cubic polynomials whose two critical points lie on the boundary of the fixed Siegel disk is a quasicircle. This locus is known as the Zakeri curve. The main step is a boundary correspondence lemma for holomorphic families of disks with uniformly quasiconformal extensions. We further prove that every capture component in this family is a quasidisk, including components attached to the Zakeri curve.

papers.title: Bistable fronts in periodic media: phase reduction and realization of circle flows
papers.abstract: We establish a phase reduction and a converse realization theorem for front dynamics in one-dimensional periodic reaction-diffusion-advection equations. For sufficiently large periods under local bistability, and sufficiently small periods when the homogenized equation admits a stationary front, we construct strictly ordered invariant front families that are normally exponentially attracting and locally complete for entire orbits. Modulo spatial-period translations, the dynamics on each family reduces exactly to a circle flow: rotations correspond to propagating pulsating fronts, equilibria to stationary fronts, and connecting orbits to transition fronts between stationary fronts. Conversely, every smooth circle flow can be realized, up to time-preserving topological conjugacy, as the quotient dynamics of such a family for a periodic, locally bistable equation with constant diffusion and no advection. Realizations with a Cantor set of stationary phases and a connecting orbit in each complementary interval illustrate the richness of front dynamics in these media. We also obtain first-order phase-velocity expansions in both period limits, quantitative propagation laws near zero frozen speed, and global exponential orbital stability of propagating pulsating fronts.

papers.title: BoundedGS: Memory-Efficient High-Resolution Training for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: High-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting training increases pixel and Gaussian-tile intersection counts, expanding rasterization caches that coexist with projection and gradient state at peak memory. A complete-view update aggregates gradients across the view; each region's forward and backward caches can be released after its contribution is collected. BoundedGS separates rasterization and projection backward passes and bounds the active local rasterization working set according to its measured load. Candidate-indexed projection and compact gradient storage address the view-level peaks exposed by this change, while CPU-assisted structure rebuilding and bounded image supply manage resources outside rendering. In a resolution sweep at a fixed count of about 6M Gaussians, the measured rendering working set stays within 1.073-1.077 GiB from 1K to 16K; at 11K, a warm pass takes 19.79 seconds versus 21.76 for full-frame execution. Across five native 5K outdoor scenes, full training reduces the mean rendering working set from 9.97 to 1.76 GiB (82.3%), retains similar reconstruction quality, and shortens training time from 36.7 to 33.9 minutes. Project page: https://xiaobin2001.github.io/BoundedGS-Web/

history_evidence.official_title: BoundedGS: Memory-Efficient High-Resolution Training for 3D Gaussian Splatting
history_evidence.official_abstract: High-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting training increases pixel and Gaussian-tile intersection counts, expanding rasterization caches that coexist with projection and gradient state at peak memory. A complete-view update aggregates gradients across the view; each region's forward and backward caches can be released after its contribution is collected. BoundedGS separates rasterization and projection backward passes and bounds the active local rasterization working set according to its measured load. Candidate-indexed projection and compact gradient storage address the view-level peaks exposed by this change, while CPU-assisted structure rebuilding and bounded image supply manage resources outside rendering. In a resolution sweep at a fixed count of about 6M Gaussians, the measured rendering working set stays within 1.073-1.077 GiB from 1K to 16K; at 11K, a warm pass takes 19.79 seconds versus 21.76 for full-frame execution. Across five native 5K outdoor scenes, full training reduces the mean rendering working set from 9.97 to 1.76 GiB (82.3%), retains similar reconstruction quality, and shortens training time from 36.7 to 33.9 minutes. papers.title: ParetoGS: High-Quality Continuous-Budget 3D Gaussian Splatting with Sparse Adapted Anchors
papers.abstract: Scalable 3D Gaussian Splatting allows one scene representation to serve different Gaussian-count budgets, yet its quality-budget curve may lag behind models optimized separately for each budget. Reducing the number of Gaussians changes both the selected members and the reconstruction tasks carried by the survivors; parameters inherited from a high-budget model may fit a low-budget representation poorly. We propose ParetoGS, which describes member changes and parameter evolution with a small set of adapted budget anchors and decodes intermediate budgets without separate optimization at every requested count. ParetoGS alternates pruning and fixed-member adaptation to build nested anchors with persistent identities, and encodes their parameter changes relative to the full model in a compact residual atlas. At decoding, it interpolates the states of shared members and gradually introduces the rendering contributions of new members, connecting sparse anchors into a continuous-budget representation. Across 13 scenes, ParetoGS attains better average PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS with fewer Gaussians than the compared prefix methods at 10% of each method's own full model. From a shared full model, it also outperforms FlexGS-imp at its trained 1%, 5%, and 10% budgets and NanoGS-imp at the 1% and 0.1% budgets. On Garden, its non-anchor quality approaches an empirical reference from independently optimized GNS models at higher retention ratios and exceeds it at some lower-budget points. Across 13 scenes, encoding reduces mean additional state from 390.0 to 85.7 MB with an average PSNR change of 0.01 dB. Project page: https://xiaobin2001.github.io/ParetoGS-Web/

papers.title: Variational Cognitive Memory Abstraction for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown remarkable success in robotic manipulation, yet their ability to execute long-horizon tasks remains limited by insufficient long- term memory modeling. Existing methods either rely on implicit temporal representations within policy networks, where historical information can be gradually diluted, or maintain explicit memory buffers that suffer from redundancy, noise accumulation, and inefficient retrieval. In this paper, we propose CogMemory, a novel variational cognitive memory framework that enables VLA systems to selectively preserve and reuse task-relevant historical information. Our approach encodes multimodal trajectories into compact latent memory representations through a selective state- space memory encoder, multi-slot temporal abstraction, and variational information compression. During action generation, dynamic cross-attention retrieval with gated fusion adaptively incorporates relevant memories into policy prediction. With merely 3.45M additional parameters, CogMemory stays lightweight and seamlessly fits both early- and intermediate-fusion VLA backbones. Extensive experiments on long-horizon robotic manipulation benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse VLA backbones.

papers.title: A marked scheme representation for Voronoi volumes in the Brownian map
papers.abstract: For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of independent volume-sampled sites in the unit-area Brownian map, we represent the negative-power transform of their ordinary Voronoi volumes as a finite sum of marked planar scheme integrals. These integrals arise from the critical asymptotics of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps. To connect them to Voronoi volumes, we use Miermont's zero-delay correspondence to interpret the labelled maps as quadrangulations with distinguished sites and then pass to the Brownian map scaling limit.

papers.title: RacerGS: Residual-Autoregressive Context for 3D Gaussian Splatting Compression
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a promising approach for fast, high-quality novel-view rendering. However, its large parameter size remains a bottleneck for storage and transmission. We propose RacerGS, a compact 3DGS compression framework that achieves scene reconstruction at significantly reduced storage sizes with preserved fidelity. To obtain compact and spatially coherent features, we design a hash projection model that projects the anchor hash encodings into compact context features. Additionally, we introduce a FiLM-modulated autoregressive GRU context model that utilizes causal dependencies among anchor feature groups and uses recurrent hidden states to refine entropy-model parameters, improving bitrate efficiency. Furthermore, we adaptively entropy-code quantized anchor-attribute residuals relative to their context-predicted means, leveraging spatial consistency to reduce symbol entropy. Overall, RacerGS achieves more than 150x compression over vanilla 3DGS and 28x over Scaffold-GS, while providing comparable rendering quality. Extensive experiments across five datasets demonstrate that RacerGS outperforms prior 3DGS compression methods in both storage reduction and rate-distortion performance.

papers.title: A Lambda Calculus Based on Quantum Logic
papers.abstract: We propose a typed lambda calculus based on quantum logic. We first present a natural deduction system for quantum logic with the Sasaki hook as its implication operation and then formulate a typed lambda calculus connected to this system through the Curry-Howard correspondence. We prove soundness and completeness of the former with respect to orthomodular lattices and strong normalization of the latter. The resulting lambda calculus has the characteristic feature that only one assumption is available in the typing derivation that serves as the premise of $λ$-abstraction. Under this restriction, ordinary currying is not available in general, but it is still possible to perform $λ$-abstraction by combining multiple assumptions into a single argument of product type and to construct a term corresponding to a deduction using the Sasaki projection.

papers.title: $(p,q)$-weighted dual curvature measures
papers.abstract: We study (p,q)-weighted dual curvature measures associated with a fixed nonnegative locally integrable Borel density satisfying a trace-regularity condition. These measures arise naturally from a variational formula for Wulff shapes. We establish the trace-regularity condition when g is pointwise α-homogeneous for some α\in R, or when g is radially non-increasing and continuous. For nontrivial even densities in either class, we prove existence results for the even version of the associated Minkowski problem under suitable assumptions. We also establish uniqueness when the prescribed measure has finite support, under a strict positivity assumption on the density and additional restrictions on the parameters. In the case of Lebesgue measure, our curvature measures reduce to those introduced by Lutwak, Yang, and Zhang, and our variational formulas recover their corresponding variational formula. For Gaussian measure, our results are related to those of Feng, Hu, and Xu, and Feng, Li, and Xu. Finally, we investigate the affine properties of the new measures and the associated mixed volumes.

papers.title: Robust Single-Parameter Point Cloud Registration using Truncated Lp Functions
papers.abstract: We propose a novel method for robust point cloud registration with only one tunable parameter. Our method, dubbed TLP, uses truncated $L_p$ functions with different values of $p$ to assign priority scores to correspondences, select the hypothesis, and refine the final model. By leveraging the robustness of truncated functions, TLP effectively handles the high outlier rates commonly encountered in real-world 3D feature matching. We also exploit GPU parallelization to evaluate hypotheses efficiently, enabling registration from thousands of correspondences in under a second on average. With only one tunable parameter, our method offers greater practicality than multi-parameter methods that require dataset-specific tuning of several parameters. Evaluations on public benchmark datasets demonstrate that TLP achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art single-parameter methods. Furthermore, it outperforms two widely used multi-parameter methods on three of the four evaluated datasets while maintaining competitive runtime.

papers.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Training a spatial VLM to answer which side an object lies on does not require it to preserve the metric displacement that determines that answer, while supervision for a distance estimate may leave categorical relations largely unconstrained. When post-training emphasizes one readout, improvements can therefore concentrate on that interface while transfer to others remains weak or even degrades; we call this observed specialization interface lock-in. ChronoReplay addresses it by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision as chronologically ordered episodes, retaining source-native targets, and balancing supervision across families. Under the same observation access, a single ChronoReplay checkpoint improves OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench, and UCS-Bench together, including a 13.41-point gain on OST-Bench, and achieves the highest three-benchmark mean among the supervision settings compared here. Same-data controls further separate the ingredients of this transfer: answer serialization redistributes gains across OST and UCS, family-balanced learning improves over ordinary joint SFT and natural turn weighting, and chronological replay exceeds a shifted-order control by about 2.41 OST points across two paired seeds. Adaptive frame selection then changes evidence access while keeping the trained model fixed, providing an additional inference-time gain at lower visual cost. Streaming spatial performance depends on what distinctions supervision preserves, how heterogeneous histories are organized during learning, and what causal evidence inference makes available at test time.

papers.title: Recovering fractal boundary dimensions from Robin eigenvalues
papers.abstract: We study Robin problems in which a small local boundary coefficient competes with the increasing surface measure of a finite-depth fractal approximation. For a fixed smooth domain, layer potentials give Green function and eigenpair expansions; contour residues and a finite-rank reduction yield a quantitative spectral-gap-dependent eigenvalue remainder. For varying Lipschitz domains, a uniform Poincaré inequality and a trace estimate with respect to normalized surface measure give a uniform ground-state expansion and a rank-one resolvent singularity as the total Robin boundary mass tends to zero. Under the boundary-resolution hypothesis and the condition on the approximation scales, ground-state measurements with known Robin coefficients recover the lower and upper Minkowski dimensions for sequences with bounded total Robin boundary mass. We describe Neumann, generalized Robin, and Dirichlet-type operator limits under the corresponding compact Mosco convergence hypotheses. Koch snowflake computations illustrate the reconstruction formulas, and an exact finite-stage area correction improves the adjacent-stage dimension estimator.

papers.title: ScheNav: Schematic-Guided Object Goal Navigation
papers.abstract: Object goal navigation requires an embodied agent to locate and reach target objects in complex environments. Humans often rely on low-cost yet informative schematic maps, such as rough sketches or directional annotations. We develop a workflow for schematic-guided embodied navigation with two components: a training-data generation pipeline and ScheNav, a closed-loop navigation framework. Our lightweight data-generation pipeline turns 2D floorplans into navigation training environments, yielding Furnished-RPLAN, a dataset of over 33k furnished layouts with paired navigation episodes and noise-controllable schematic maps. ScheNav turns rough schematic guidance into exploration and stopping decisions by using SchemaField, a learned spatial module that fuses the guidance with accumulated observations and predicts spatial value fields. The framework updates these fields as exploration proceeds, with trajectory-based training and a cross-frame consistency objective supporting coherent guidance across changing viewpoints. ScheNav learns to use schematic guidance entirely from simulated floorplans and transfers this ability to unseen embodied environments. Experiments show improved navigation success and path efficiency across schematic maps, goal ellipses, and pointed directions, together with tolerance to the tested schematic perturbations and omissions. Together, these results demonstrate that rough schematic guidance offers a practical way to improve embodied navigation.

history_evidence.official_title: ScheNav: Schematic-Guided Object Goal Navigation
history_evidence.official_abstract: Object goal navigation requires an embodied agent to locate and reach target objects in complex environments. Humans often rely on low-cost yet informative schematic maps, such as rough sketches or directional annotations. We develop a workflow for schematic-guided embodied navigation with two components: a training-data generation pipeline and ScheNav, a closed-loop navigation framework. Our lightweight data-generation pipeline turns 2D floorplans into navigation training environments, yielding Furnished-RPLAN, a dataset of over 33k furnished layouts with paired navigation episodes and noise-controllable schematic maps. ScheNav turns rough schematic guidance into exploration and stopping decisions by using SchemaField, a learned spatial module that fuses the guidance with accumulated observations and predicts spatial value fields. The framework updates these fields as exploration proceeds, with trajectory-based training and a cross-frame consistency objective supporting coherent guidance across changing viewpoints. ScheNav learns to use schematic guidance entirely from simulated floorplans and transfers this ability to unseen embodied environments. Experiments show improved navigation success and path efficiency across schematic maps, goal ellipses, and pointed directions, together with tolerance to the tested schematic perturbations and omissions. Together, these results demonstrate that rough schematic guidance offers a practical way to improve embodied navigation.

papers.title: Robust Observability for Schrödinger Equations with Singular Potentials on 2D Compact Hyperbolic Surfaces
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the robustness of quantum observability on compact hyperbolic surfaces subject to $L^q$ potential perturbations with $2<q\leq \infty$. Since $L^q$ regularity is strictly subcritical in dimension two, for every non-empty open set $Ω\subset M$ and $T>0$, the solution of $(i\partial_t+Δ-V)u=0$ satisfies the space-time observability estimate $$ \|u_0\|_{L^2(M)}^2 \leq C\int_0^T \|e^{-it(-Δ+V)}u_0\|_{L^2(Ω)}^2\,dt. $$ A cornerstone of our analysis is Sogge's spectral cluster estimate, which allows us to obtain refined spectrally localized semiclassical Strichartz estimates adapted to rough potentials and to show that the potential's contribution vanishes in the propagation of semiclassical measures. The full-support property of invariant semiclassical measures on hyperbolic surfaces associated with the eigenfunctions then yields the desired observability by contradiction. By the Hilbert Uniqueness Method, the corresponding internal controllability result follows.

papers.title: Virtual defect mediated quantum melting in supersolids
papers.abstract: The current understanding of supersolid melting is largely based on mean-field theories predicting that such transitions arise from a structural energy minimization mechanism. Here, we show that soft-core quasi-one-dimensional supersolids stabilized by a shallow external lattice can instead melt at zero temperature into a superfluid phase with quasi-long-range positional order through the proliferation of virtual soliton--antisoliton pairs, leading to a Kosterlitz--Thouless transition. We derive the corresponding Renormalization Group equations from first principles and use them to determine the critical properties of the system. Remarkably, the proliferation of topological defects near criticality strongly renormalizes both the density modulation and the superfluidity behavior. The transition described is intrinsically a beyond mean-field effect, since the external lattice produces only a smooth crossover between weakly and strongly modulated states at the mean-field level.
